title.zh: 卷六十三 列傳第五十一: 周惠達 馮景 蘇綽
title.en: Volume 63 Biographies 51: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, Su Chao
title.raw: 卷六十三 列傳第五十一: 周惠達 馮景 蘇綽 Volume 63 Biographies 51: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, Su Chao

sentences.zh: 周惠達 馮景 蘇綽

translations.literal: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, Su Chuo
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, and Su Chuo

sentences.zh: 列傳第五十一

translations.literal: Biographies fifty-one
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 51

sentences.zh: 周惠達馮景蘇綽子威從兄亮

translations.literal: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, Su Chuo; Su Wei; Su Liang, Su Chuo's older cousin
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida, Feng Jing, and Su Chuo; Su Wei; Su Liang, Su Chuo's older cousin

sentences.zh: 周惠達，字懷文，章武文安人也。

translations.literal: Zhou Huida, style name Huaiwen, was a man of Wen'an in Zhangwu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Huida, courtesy name Huaiwen, was a native of Wen'an in Zhangwu.

sentences.zh: 父信，曆樂鄉、平舒、成平三縣令，皆以廉能稱。

translations.literal: His father Xin successively served as magistrate of Lexiang, Pingshu, and Chengping—three counties—and in each was known for integrity and competence.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xin served in turn as magistrate of Lexiang, Pingshu, and Chengping, and in all three posts was praised for integrity and ability.

sentences.zh: 惠達幼有節操，好讀書，美容貌。

translations.literal: From youth Huida had integrity of character, loved reading, and had a handsome appearance.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Huida showed moral resolve, loved books, and was handsome in appearance.

sentences.zh: 魏齊王蕭寶夤為瀛州刺史，召惠達及河間馮景同在閣下，甚禮之。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi of Wei, was Governor of Yingzhou, he summoned Huida and Feng Jing of Hejian to serve together in his secretariat and treated them with great respect.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi of Wei, became Governor of Yingzhou, he summoned Huida and Feng Jing of Hejian to his staff and honored them greatly.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤還明，惠達隨入洛陽。

translations.literal: When Baoyin returned to court, Huida followed him into Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin returned to the capital, Huida accompanied him to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 寶夤西征，惠達復隨入關。

translations.literal: When Baoyin marched west on campaign, Huida again followed him through the Pass.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin campaigned west, Huida again followed him into the Pass region.

sentences.zh: 寶夤除雍州刺史，今惠達使洛陽。

translations.literal: Baoyin was appointed Governor of Yongzhou and sent Huida on a mission to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was made Governor of Yongzhou and dispatched Huida on an embassy to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 未還，而寶夤謀反聞于京師。

translations.literal: Before he returned, word reached the capital that Baoyin was plotting rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Before Huida returned, news of Baoyin's planned rebellion reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 有司以惠達是其行人，將執之。

translations.literal: The authorities, holding that Huida had been his emissary, were about to arrest him.
translations.idiomatic: The authorities, reasoning that Huida had been Baoyin's envoy, were preparing to arrest him.

sentences.zh: 惠達乃私馳還。

translations.literal: Huida then secretly rode back in haste.
translations.idiomatic: Huida then secretly galloped back.

sentences.zh: 至潼關，遇大使楊侃。

translations.literal: At Tong Pass he met the imperial envoy Yang Kan.
translations.idiomatic: At Tong Pass he encountered the imperial envoy Yang Kan.

sentences.zh: 侃謂曰：「何為故入獸口？」

translations.literal: Kan said to him, "Why deliberately walk into the mouth of a beast?
translations.idiomatic: Kan said to him, "Why go out of your way to walk into the jaws of a beast?

sentences.zh: 惠達曰：「蕭王必為左右所誤，今往，庶其改圖。」

translations.literal: Huida said, "Prince Xiao must have been misled by those around him; if I go now, perhaps he will change his plans."
translations.idiomatic: Huida replied, "Prince Xiao must have been led astray by his attendants; if I go now, perhaps he will reconsider."

sentences.zh: 及至，寶夤反形已露，不可彌縫。

translations.literal: When he arrived, Baoyin's rebellious intent was already exposed and could no longer be concealed.
translations.idiomatic: But when he arrived, Baoyin's rebellion was already plain and could no longer be patched over.

sentences.zh: 遂用惠達為光祿勳、中書舍人。

translations.literal: Baoyin then appointed Huida Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Palace Attendant Drafting Documents.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin then made Huida Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Palace Attendant in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 寶夤既敗，唯惠達等數人從之。

translations.literal: After Baoyin was defeated, only Huida and a few others followed him.
translations.idiomatic: After Baoyin's defeat, only Huida and a handful of others stayed with him.

sentences.zh: 寶夤語惠達曰：「人生富貴，左右咸言盡節，及遭厄難，乃知歲寒也。」

translations.literal: Baoyin said to Huida, "In life's prosperity, those around you all speak of utter loyalty; only when hardship strikes does one learn what the cold of winter reveals."
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin said to Huida, "When life is rich and honored, everyone around you claims total loyalty; only in adversity do you discover who truly endures the winter cold."

sentences.zh: 賀拔嶽為關中大行，惠達為嶽府屬。

translations.literal: Heba Yue was Grand Commissioner of Guanzhong, and Huida served on Yue's staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue became Grand Commissioner of Guanzhong, Huida served in his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 岳為侯莫陳悅所害，惠達遁入漢陽之麥積崖。

translations.literal: Yue was killed by Houmo Chen Yue; Huida fled to Maiji Cliff in Hanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue was murdered by Houmo Chen Yue, and Huida fled to Maiji Cliff in Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 悅平，歸於周文帝。

translations.literal: After Yue was suppressed, Huida submitted to Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue was defeated, Huida went over to Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 文帝復以為府司馬，便委任焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen again made him headquarters marshal and at once entrusted him with real authority.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen again appointed him headquarters marshal and immediately gave him substantive responsibility.

sentences.zh: 周文帝為大將軍、大行台，以惠達為行台尚書、大將軍府司馬，封文安縣子。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou became Grand General and Grand Commissioner, he appointed Huida Director of the Commission Secretariat and Grand General's Headquarters Marshal, and enfeoffed him as Viscount of Wen'an County.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was made Grand General and Grand Commissioner, he appointed Huida Director of the Commission Secretariat and headquarters marshal, enfeoffing him as Viscount of Wen'an County.

sentences.zh: 周文出鎮華州，留惠達知後事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen went out to garrison Huazhou, he left Huida in charge of rear affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen went to take command at Huazhou, he left Huida to manage affairs behind the lines.

sentences.zh: 時既承喪亂，庶事多闕。

translations.literal: The times had just passed through chaos and ruin, and many affairs were still neglected.
translations.idiomatic: The realm had just emerged from chaos and ruin, and countless matters remained undone.

sentences.zh: 惠達營造戎仗，儲積倉糧，簡閱士馬，以濟軍國之務，甚為朝廷所稱。

translations.literal: Huida saw to military equipment, stockpiled grain in granaries, reviewed troops and horses, and handled matters urgent to army and state—all much praised by the court.
translations.idiomatic: Huida organized weapons and armor, filled the granaries, inspected troops and horses, and met the urgent needs of army and state—work the court praised highly.

sentences.zh: 後拜中書令，進爵為公。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Palace Director and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made Palace Director and raised in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 大統四年，兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Datong he additionally served as Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Datong he also held the post of Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年，周文與魏文帝東討，令惠達輔魏太子居守，總留台事。

translations.literal: That year Emperor Wen of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Wei marched east on campaign; Huida was left to assist the Wei crown prince in holding the capital and oversee all affairs of the remaining administration.
translations.idiomatic: That same year, when Emperor Wen of Zhou and Emperor Wen of Wei marched east, Huida was left to assist the Wei crown prince in defending the capital and to oversee all remaining government affairs.

sentences.zh: 及芒山失律，人情駭動。

translations.literal: When disaster struck at Mangshan, public sentiment was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: When the army met defeat at Mangshan, the people were shaken with alarm.

sentences.zh: 趙青雀據長安子城反，惠達奉太子出渭橋北以禦之。

translations.literal: Zhao Qingque seized the inner city of Chang'an and rebelled; Huida escorted the crown prince north of the Wei Bridge to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Qingque seized the inner city of Chang'an and rose in rebellion; Huida escorted the crown prince north of the Wei Bridge to oppose him.

sentences.zh: 軍還，青雀等誅。

translations.literal: When the army returned, Qingque and his followers were executed.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, Qingque and his followers were put to death.

sentences.zh: 拜吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為右僕射。

translations.literal: After some time he again became Vice Director of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: After some time he again became Vice Director of the Right.

sentences.zh: 自關右草創，禮樂缺然。

translations.literal: Since the founding of rule west of the Pass, rites and music had been largely absent.
translations.idiomatic: From the time the regime was first established west of the Pass, rites and music had been sorely lacking.

sentences.zh: 惠達與禮官損益舊章，是以儀軌稍備。

translations.literal: Huida worked with the ritual officials to revise the old regulations, and thereby court ceremony gradually became complete.
translations.idiomatic: Huida worked with the ritual officials to adapt the old regulations, and court ceremony gradually took shape.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝因朝奏樂，顧謂惠達曰：「此卿功也。」

translations.literal: At an imperial audience when music was performed, Emperor Wen of Wei turned to Huida and said, "This is your achievement.
translations.idiomatic: At court, while music was performed, Emperor Wen of Wei turned to Huida and said, "This is your doing.

sentences.zh: 惠達雖居顯職，性廉退，善下人，盡心勤公，愛拔良士，以此皆敬而附之。

translations.literal: Though Huida held high office, he was by nature modest and retiring, gracious to those below him, devoted in public service, and eager to promote worthy men—on these accounts all honored and attached themselves to him.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huida held high office, he was modest by nature, kind to those beneath him, devoted in public service, and eager to lift up worthy men; for these reasons all respected and rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 薨，子題嗣。

translations.literal: When he died, his son Ti succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, his son Ti inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，以惠達著績前代，追封蕭國公。

translations.literal: In the early Kaihuang reign of Sui, because of Huida's distinguished record in the previous dynasty, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kaihuang era of Sui, because of Huida's distinguished service under the previous dynasty, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Xiao.

sentences.zh: 馮景，字長明，河間武垣人也。

translations.literal: Feng Jing, style name Changming, was a man of Wuyuan in Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Jing, courtesy name Changming, was a native of Wuyuan in Hejian.

sentences.zh: 父傑，為伏與令。

translations.literal: His father Jie served as magistrate of Fuyu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jie was magistrate of Fuyu.

sentences.zh: 景少與周惠達友，俱以客從蕭寶夤。

translations.literal: In youth Jing was friendly with Zhou Huida; both followed Xiao Baoyin as clients.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jing was close friends with Zhou Huida; both followed Xiao Baoyin as retainers.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後為尚書右僕射，引景領尚書都令史。

translations.literal: Later Baoyin became Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat and brought Jing in as Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Baoyin became Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat, he brought Jing in as Chief Clerk of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 正光中，寶夤為關西大行台，景又為行台都令史。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era Baoyin was Grand Commissioner of Guanxi; Jing again served as Chief Clerk of the Commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguang era, when Baoyin was Grand Commissioner of Guanxi, Jing again served as Chief Clerk of the Commission.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤敗還長安，或議歸罪闕下，或言留州立功。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated and returned to Chang'an, some urged accepting blame at court while others said he should stay in the province and achieve merit.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was defeated and returned to Chang'an, some argued that he should go to court and accept punishment, while others said he should remain in the province and win merit.

sentences.zh: 景曰：「擁兵不還，此罪將大。」

translations.literal: Jing said, "To hold troops and not return—this offense will be grave.
translations.idiomatic: Jing said, "If you keep your army and refuse to return, the offense will be grave.

sentences.zh: 寶夤不從，遂反。

translations.literal: Baoyin did not listen and then rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin would not heed him and then rebelled.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤平，景方得還洛。

translations.literal: After Baoyin was suppressed, Jing was finally able to return to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Baoyin was suppressed was Jing able to return to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷聞景有諫言，故不罪之。

translations.literal: The court heard that Jing had offered remonstrance, and therefore did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: The court learned that Jing had offered remonstrance, and therefore did not punish him.

sentences.zh: 後事賀拔嶽為行台郎。

translations.literal: Later he served Heba Yue as a Commission secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served Heba Yue as a secretary on the Commission staff.

sentences.zh: 岳使景詣齊神武，察其行事。

translations.literal: Yue sent Jing to Gao Huan to observe his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Yue sent Jing to Gao Huan to observe his behavior.

sentences.zh: 神武聞嶽使至，甚有喜色，問曰：「賀拔公詎憶吾邪？」

translations.literal: When Huan heard that Yue's envoy had arrived, he showed great pleasure and asked, "Does Lord Heba really remember me?
translations.idiomatic: When Huan heard that Yue's envoy had arrived, his face brightened with pleasure, and he asked, "Does Lord Heba truly remember me?

sentences.zh: 即與景歃血，托岳為兄弟。

translations.literal: He immediately drank blood with Jing in oath, entrusting Yue as a sworn brother.
translations.idiomatic: He at once drank blood with Jing in oath, treating Yue as a sworn brother.

sentences.zh: 景還，以狀報嶽。

translations.literal: Jing returned and reported this in detail to Yue.
translations.idiomatic: Jing returned and reported the full account to Yue.

sentences.zh: 嶽曰：「此奸有餘，而實不足。

translations.literal: Yue said, "That man is more cunning than solid.
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "That man has cunning to spare but substance in short supply.

sentences.zh: 自古王臣無私盟者也，吾料之熟矣。」

translations.literal: From antiquity subject and sovereign have never sworn private oaths together—I have already judged him thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, ministers and rulers have never sworn private oaths together—I have already taken his measure.

sentences.zh: 岳北合費也頭，東引紇豆陵伊利，西總侯莫陳悅、河州刺史梁景睿及酋渠為盟誓，共會平涼，移軍東下。

translations.literal: Yue allied with the north to join the Fei Yetou, eastward drew in Kedouling Yili, westward gathered Houmo Chen Yue, Liang Jingrui Governor of Hezhou, and tribal chiefs in holy oath; they assembled at Pingliang and moved the army east.
translations.idiomatic: Yue allied in the north with the Fei Yetou, drew Kedouling Yili in from the east, and in the west rallied Houmo Chen Yue, Liang Jingrui the Governor of Hezhou, and tribal chiefs in sworn alliance; they met at Pingliang and moved the army eastward.

sentences.zh: 懼有專任之嫌，使景啟孝武帝。

translations.literal: Fearing suspicion of acting on his own authority, he had Jing report to Emperor Xiaowu.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing the suspicion of acting on his own authority, he had Jing report to Emperor Xiaowu.

sentences.zh: 帝甚悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 又為岳大都督府從事中郎。

translations.literal: Jing also served as Drafting Officer in Yue's Grand Commander headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He also served as Drafting Officer in Yue's Grand Commander headquarters.

sentences.zh: 後侯莫陳悅平，周文使景于京師告捷。

translations.literal: Later, after Houmo Chen Yue was suppressed, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Jing to the capital to announce the victory.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Houmo Chen Yue was defeated, Emperor Wen of Zhou sent Jing to the capital to announce the victory.

sentences.zh: 帝有西遷意，因問關中事勢。

translations.literal: The emperor had in mind moving west; he therefore asked about the military situation in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already thinking of moving west, and therefore asked about conditions in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 景勸帝西遷。

translations.literal: Jing urged the emperor to move west.
translations.idiomatic: Jing urged the emperor to move west.

sentences.zh: 後以迎孝武功，封高陽縣伯，除散騎常侍、行台尚書。

translations.literal: Later, for merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang County and appointed Regular Attendant at the Imperial Gate and Acting Director of the Commission Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, for his merit in welcoming Emperor Xiaowu, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang County and appointed Regular Attendant and Acting Director of the Commission Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大統初，詔行涇州事，卒於官。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong an edict appointed him to administer Jingzhou affairs; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Datong he was ordered to administer Jingzhou affairs and died in office.

sentences.zh: 蘇綽，字令綽，武功人，魏侍中則之九世孫也。

translations.literal: Su Chuo, style name Lingchuo, was a man of Wugong—the ninth-generation descendant of Su Ze, who had been Palace Attendant of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Su Chuo, courtesy name Lingchuo, was a native of Wugong and the ninth-generation descendant of Su Ze, who had served as Palace Attendant of Wei.

sentences.zh: 累世二千石。

translations.literal: For generations his family had held offices of two-thousand-dan rank.
translations.idiomatic: For generations his family had held offices of two-thousand-dan rank.

sentences.zh: 父協，武功郡守。

translations.literal: His father Xie was Prefect of Wugong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xie was Prefect of Wugong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 綽少好學，博覽群書，尤善算術。

translations.literal: From youth Chuo loved learning, read widely among books, and was especially skilled in calculation.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Chuo loved learning, read widely, and was especially skilled in mathematics.

sentences.zh: 從兄讓為汾州刺史，周帝餞於都門外。

translations.literal: His older cousin Rang was appointed Governor of Fenzhou; the Emperor of Zhou saw him off outside the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: His older cousin Rang was appointed Governor of Fenzhou, and the Emperor of Zhou saw him off outside the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 臨別，謂曰：「卿家子弟之中，誰可任用者？」

translations.literal: At parting he asked, "Among the young men of your clan, whom can you recommend for service?
translations.idiomatic: At parting he asked, "Among the young men of your family, whom can you recommend for service?

sentences.zh: 讓因薦綽。

translations.literal: Rang thereupon recommended Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Rang thereupon recommended Chuo.

sentences.zh: 周文乃召為行台郎中。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou then summoned him as Drafting Officer of the Commission.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou then summoned him as a Drafting Officer on the Commission staff.

sentences.zh: 在官歲餘，未見知。

translations.literal: More than a year in office passed before he was noticed.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year passed in office before anyone took notice of him.

sentences.zh: 然諸曹疑事，皆詢於綽而後定。

translations.literal: Yet whenever the various bureaus had doubtful cases, all consulted Chuo before deciding.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever the various bureaus faced doubtful matters, all consulted Chuo before deciding.

sentences.zh: 所行公文，綽又為之條式。

translations.literal: For official documents issued from the office, Chuo also set down the forms and standards.
translations.idiomatic: For official documents issued from the office, Chuo also established the forms and standards.

sentences.zh: 台中咸稱其能。

translations.literal: Everyone in the Commission praised his ability.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone in the Commission praised his competence.

sentences.zh: 周文與僕射周惠達論事，惠達不能對，請出外議之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou discussed affairs with Vice Director Zhou Huida, Huida could not reply and asked to withdraw to consult elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou discussed affairs with Vice Director Zhou Huida, Huida could not answer and asked to withdraw to consult further.

sentences.zh: 乃召綽，告以其事，綽即為量定。

translations.literal: He then summoned Chuo, told him the matter, and Chuo at once worked out the proper measure.
translations.idiomatic: He then summoned Chuo, explained the matter, and Chuo at once worked out the proper course.

sentences.zh: 惠達入呈，周文稱善，謂曰：「誰與卿為此議者？」

translations.literal: Huida entered and presented it; Emperor Wen of Zhou commended it and asked, "Who worked out this plan with you?
translations.idiomatic: Huida went in and presented the answer; Emperor Wen praised it and asked, "Who worked out this plan with you?

sentences.zh: 惠達以綽對，因稱其有王佐才。

translations.literal: Huida named Chuo and thereby praised him as having the talent of a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Huida named Chuo and praised him as having the talent of a chief minister.

sentences.zh: 周文曰：「吾亦聞之久矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said, "I have heard of him for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen said, "I have heard of him for a long time.

sentences.zh: 尋除著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was appointed Assistant Drafting Officer in the History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward Chuo was appointed Assistant Drafting Officer in the History Office.

sentences.zh: 屬周文與公卿往昆明池觀漁，行至城西漢故倉地，顧問左右，莫有知者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou went with the public officials to Kunming Pool to watch fishing, as they passed west of the city at the site of the old Han granary, he looked about and asked those around him, but none knew.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou went with the high officials to Kunming Pool to watch fishing, they passed west of the city at the site of the old Han granary; he looked around and asked his attendants, but none knew.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「蘇綽博物多通，請問之。」

translations.literal: Someone said, "Su Chuo is widely learned and knows much—let us ask him.
translations.idiomatic: Someone said, "Su Chuo is widely learned—let us ask him.

sentences.zh: 周文乃召綽問，具以狀對。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen then summoned Chuo and questioned him; he answered fully according to the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen then summoned Chuo and questioned him; he answered in full detail.

sentences.zh: 周文大悅，因問天地造化之始，歷代興亡之跡。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased and then asked about the beginning of heaven and earth's creation and the traces of successive rises and falls of dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was greatly pleased and then asked about the origins of heaven and earth and the rise and fall of successive dynasties.

sentences.zh: 綽既有口辯，應對如流。

translations.literal: Chuo, being eloquent in speech, answered as smoothly as flowing water.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was eloquent, and his replies flowed as smoothly as water.

sentences.zh: 周文益嘉之，乃與綽並馬徐行至池，竟不設網罟而還。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen was all the more delighted; he rode side by side with Chuo at an easy pace to the pool and returned without setting nets or traps.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen was all the more delighted; he rode side by side with Chuo at an easy pace to the pool and returned without ever setting nets or traps.

sentences.zh: 遂留綽至夜，問以政道，臥而聽之。

translations.literal: He kept Chuo until night and questioned him on principles of governance, listening while reclining.
translations.idiomatic: He kept Chuo until night, questioning him on principles of governance while reclining and listening.

sentences.zh: 綽於是指陳帝王之道，兼述申、韓之要。

translations.literal: Chuo thereupon set forth the way of emperors and kings, and together expounded the essentials of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo thereupon set forth the way of emperors and kings and also explained the essentials of Shen Buhai and Han Fei.

sentences.zh: 周文乃起，整衣危坐，不覺膝之前席。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen then rose, straightened his robes, and sat formally upright—unconsciously his knees moved forward beyond the mat's edge.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen then rose, straightened his robes, and sat upright with formal attention—before he knew it his knees had moved forward beyond the edge of the mat.

sentences.zh: 語遂達曙不厭。

translations.literal: Their talk lasted until dawn without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: Their conversation lasted until dawn without either tiring.

sentences.zh: 詰朝，謂周惠達曰：「蘇綽真奇士，吾方任之以政。」

translations.literal: The next morning he said to Zhou Huida, "Su Chuo is truly an extraordinary man; I am about to entrust him with governance.
translations.idiomatic: The next morning he said to Zhou Huida, "Su Chuo is truly an extraordinary man; I am about to entrust him with governance.

sentences.zh: 即拜大行台左丞，參典機密。

translations.literal: He at once appointed him Left Assistant Director of the Grand Commission, with participation in secret affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: He at once appointed Chuo Left Assistant Director of the Grand Commission, with a role in confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 自是寵遇日隆。

translations.literal: From then on favor toward him grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: From then on imperial favor toward him grew daily.

sentences.zh: 綽始制文案程式，硃出墨入，及計帳、戶籍之法。

translations.literal: Chuo first established the forms for written documents—red for outgoing, black for incoming—and methods for ledger accounts and household registers.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo first established the forms for written documents—red for outgoing, black for incoming—and the methods for ledger accounts and household registers.

sentences.zh: 大統三年，齊神武三道入寇，諸將咸欲分兵禦之，獨綽意與周文同。

translations.literal: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan of Qi invaded on three routes; all the generals wished to divide the army to resist, but only Chuo's view agreed with Emperor Wen of Zhou's.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Datong, Gao Huan of Qi invaded on three routes; the generals all wanted to split the army to resist him, but only Chuo agreed with Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 遂並力拒竇泰，擒之於潼關。

translations.literal: They then combined forces to resist Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: They then united their strength to oppose Dou Tai and captured him at Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 封美陽縣伯。

translations.literal: Chuo was enfeoffed as Baron of Meiyang County.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed as Baron of Meiyang County.

sentences.zh: 十一年，授大行台度支尚書，領著作，兼司農卿。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was appointed Director of Revenue of the Grand Commission, concurrently head of the History Office, and also Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was made Director of Revenue of the Grand Commission, concurrently head of the History Office, and also Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 周文方欲革易時政，務弘強國富人之道，故綽得盡其智能，贊成其事。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou was then seeking to reform current policy and promote the way of strengthening the state and enriching the people; therefore Chuo was able to deploy his full intelligence and assist in the undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou was then intent on reforming government and promoting the path of strengthening the state and enriching the people, so Chuo was able to apply his full talents and help bring it about.

sentences.zh: 減官員，置二長，並置屯田以資軍國。

translations.literal: He reduced officials, established the two-head system, and also established military colonies to support army and state.
translations.idiomatic: He reduced the number of officials, established the two-head system, and set up military colonies to supply army and state.

sentences.zh: 又為六條詔書，奏施行之。

translations.literal: He also drafted the Six Edicts and memorialized the throne to put them into effect.
translations.idiomatic: He also drafted the Six Edicts and submitted them for implementation.

sentences.zh: 其一，先修心，曰：

translations.literal: The first: first cultivate the heart. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The first edict, on cultivating the heart first, reads:

sentences.zh: 凡今之方伯守令，皆受命天朝，出臨下國，論其尊貴，並古之諸侯也。

translations.literal: All the regional governors and magistrates of today receive their commissions from the imperial court and go forth to govern subordinate states; in rank and dignity they are all like the feudal lords of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: All the regional governors and magistrates of today receive their commissions from the imperial court and go forth to govern the realm; in rank and dignity they are the equals of the feudal lords of old.

sentences.zh: 是以前代帝王，每稱共理天下者唯良宰守耳。

translations.literal: Therefore emperors of former ages always said that those who jointly govern the realm are none other than good magistrates and governors.
translations.idiomatic: That is why emperors of former ages always said that those who jointly govern the realm are none other than capable magistrates and governors.

sentences.zh: 明知百僚卿尹雖各有所司，然其理人之本，莫若守宰之最重也。

translations.literal: It is clearly understood that though the hundred officials and ministers each have their duties, the foundation of governing the people lies above all in governors and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: It is well understood that though the hundred officials and ministers each have their duties, the foundation of governing the people lies above all with governors and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 凡理人之體，當先理已心，心者一身之主，百行之本。

translations.literal: The substance of governing people is that one must first govern one's own heart; the heart is master of the whole person and root of all conduct.
translations.idiomatic: The essence of governing people is to govern one's own heart first; the heart is master of the whole person and the root of all conduct.

sentences.zh: 心不清靜，則思慮妄生。

translations.literal: If the heart is not clear and tranquil, reckless thoughts arise.
translations.idiomatic: If the heart is not clear and calm, reckless thoughts arise.

sentences.zh: 思慮妄生，則見理不明。

translations.literal: When reckless thoughts arise, one's perception of principle is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: When reckless thoughts arise, one's grasp of principle grows unclear.

sentences.zh: 見理不明，則是非謬亂。

translations.literal: When one's perception of principle is unclear, right and wrong become confused and disordered.
translations.idiomatic: When one's grasp of principle is unclear, right and wrong become confused.

sentences.zh: 是非既亂，則一身不能自理，安能理人也？

translations.literal: Once right and wrong are disordered, one cannot even govern oneself—how then can one govern others?
translations.idiomatic: Once right and wrong are in disorder, one cannot even govern oneself—how then can one govern others?

sentences.zh: 是以理人之要，在於清心而已。

translations.literal: Therefore the key to governing people lies simply in purifying the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the key to governing people lies simply in purifying the heart.

sentences.zh: 夫所謂清心者，非不貪貨財之謂，乃欲使心氣清和，志意端靜。

translations.literal: What is meant by purifying the heart is not merely not coveting goods and wealth, but making the heart's qi clear and harmonious and one's will upright and tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: What is meant by purifying the heart is not merely refraining from coveting wealth, but keeping the spirit clear and harmonious and one's intentions upright and calm.

sentences.zh: 心和志靜，則邪僻之慮無因而作。

translations.literal: When heart and will are harmonious and tranquil, perverse thoughts have no occasion to arise.
translations.idiomatic: When heart and will are harmonious and calm, perverse thoughts have no occasion to arise.

sentences.zh: 邪僻不作，則凡所思念無不皆得至公之理。

translations.literal: When perversity does not arise, every thought one has can attain the principle of utmost fairness.
translations.idiomatic: When perversity does not arise, every thought one has can attain the principle of utmost fairness.

sentences.zh: 率至公之理以臨其人，則彼下人孰不從化？

translations.literal: If one applies the principle of utmost fairness in dealing with people, which of those beneath will not follow and be transformed?
translations.idiomatic: If one applies the principle of utmost fairness in dealing with people, which of those beneath will not follow and be transformed?

sentences.zh: 是以稱理人之本，先在理心。

translations.literal: Therefore it is said that the foundation of governing people lies first in governing the heart.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore it is said that the foundation of governing people lies first in governing the heart.

sentences.zh: 其次又在理身。

translations.literal: Next comes governing the person.
translations.idiomatic: Next comes governing one's own person.

sentences.zh: 凡人君之身者，乃百姓之表，一國之的也。

translations.literal: The person of a ruler is the model for the common people and the target for the whole state.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler's own person is the model for the common people and the target at which the whole state aims.

sentences.zh: 表不正，不可求直影；

translations.literal: If the model is not straight, one cannot expect a straight shadow;
translations.idiomatic: If the model is not straight, one cannot expect a straight shadow;

sentences.zh: 的不明，不可責射中。

translations.literal: if the target is not clear, one cannot demand a hit.
translations.idiomatic: if the target is not clear, one cannot demand a bull's-eye.

sentences.zh: 今君身不能自理，而望理百姓，是猶曲表而求直影也；

translations.literal: If today the ruler cannot govern his own person yet hopes to govern the people, it is like setting up a crooked model and expecting a straight shadow;
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler today cannot govern his own person yet hopes to govern the people, it is like setting up a crooked model and expecting a straight shadow;

sentences.zh: 君行不能自修，而欲百姓修行者，是猶無的而責射中也。

translations.literal: if the ruler's conduct cannot be self-cultivated yet he wants the people to cultivate themselves, it is like having no target yet demanding a hit.
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler's conduct cannot be self-cultivated yet he wants the people to cultivate themselves, it is like having no target yet demanding a bull's-eye.

sentences.zh: 故為人君者，必心如清水，形如白玉，躬行仁義，躬行孝悌，躬行忠信，躬行禮讓，躬行廉平，躬行儉約，然後繼之以無倦，加之以明察。

translations.literal: Therefore one who is a ruler must have a heart like clear water and a form like white jade; personally practice benevolence and righteousness, filial piety and brotherly duty, loyalty and trustworthiness, ritual and deference, integrity and fairness, thrift and moderation; then continue without weariness and add clear discernment.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a ruler must keep a heart like clear water and a bearing like white jade; personally practice benevolence and righteousness, filial piety and brotherly duty, loyalty and trustworthiness, ritual and deference, integrity and fairness, and thrift and moderation; then continue without weariness and add clear discernment.

sentences.zh: 行此八者以訓其人。

translations.literal: Practice these eight to instruct the people.
translations.idiomatic: Practice these eight virtues to instruct the people.

sentences.zh: 是以其人畏而愛之，則而象之，不待家教日見而自興行矣。

translations.literal: Then the people will fear and love him, take him as a rule and imitate him; without waiting for household instruction, good conduct will arise of itself day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Then the people will revere and love him, take him as their model and imitate him; without waiting for household instruction, good conduct will arise of itself day by day.

sentences.zh: 其二，敦教化，曰：

translations.literal: The second: promote moral transformation. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The second edict, on promoting moral transformation, reads:

sentences.zh: 天地之性，唯人為貴。

translations.literal: Among the natures of heaven and earth, only humanity is noble.
translations.idiomatic: Among the natures of heaven and earth, only humanity is noble.

sentences.zh: 明其有中和之心，仁恕之行，異于木石，不同禽獸，故貴之耳。

translations.literal: Clearly it possesses a heart of harmony and balance and conduct of benevolence and forbearance, different from wood and stone and not the same as birds and beasts—therefore it is held noble.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly humanity possesses a heart of harmony and conduct of benevolence and forbearance, different from wood and stone and not the same as birds and beasts—that is why it is held noble.

sentences.zh: 然性無常守，隨化而遷。

translations.literal: Yet nature has no fixed constancy and shifts with transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet human nature has no fixed constancy and shifts with what shapes it.

sentences.zh: 化于敦樸者則質直，化於澆偽者則浮薄。

translations.literal: Those transformed by honest simplicity become plain and upright; those transformed by shallow falsity become frivolous and thin.
translations.idiomatic: Those shaped by honest simplicity become plain and upright; those shaped by shallow falsity become frivolous and corrupt.

sentences.zh: 浮薄者則衰弊之風，質直者則淳和之俗。

translations.literal: The frivolous produce winds of decline and decay; the plain and upright produce customs of purity and harmony.
translations.idiomatic: The frivolous produce winds of decline and decay; the plain and upright produce customs of purity and harmony.

sentences.zh: 衰弊則禍亂交興，淳和則天下自治。

translations.literal: Decline and decay bring disaster and rebellion in succession; purity and harmony bring self-governance under heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Decline and decay bring disaster and rebellion in succession; purity and harmony bring self-governance under heaven.

sentences.zh: 自古安危興亡，無不皆由所化也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, security and danger, rise and fall—none have failed to depend on what people were transformed by.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity, security and danger, rise and fall—none have failed to depend on what shaped the people.

sentences.zh: 然世道彫喪，已數百年。

translations.literal: Yet the ways of the world have withered and decayed for several hundred years already.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ways of the world have withered and decayed for several hundred years already.

sentences.zh: 大亂滋甚，且二十載。

translations.literal: Great chaos has grown ever worse for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Great chaos has grown ever worse for nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 人不見德，唯兵革是聞；

translations.literal: People see no virtue; they hear only of arms and war;
translations.idiomatic: People hear nothing of virtue, only of arms and war;

sentences.zh: 上無教化，唯刑罰是用。

translations.literal: above there is no moral transformation; only punishments are employed.
translations.idiomatic: Above there is no moral transformation; only punishments are employed.

sentences.zh: 而中興始爾，大難未弭，加之以師旅，因之以饑饉，凡百草創，率多權宜。

translations.literal: Yet the restoration has only just begun, great calamity is not yet stilled, and to this are added armies on campaign and famine in succession; in every matter newly established, expedients have mostly prevailed.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the restoration has only just begun, great calamity is not yet stilled, and to this are added armies on campaign and famine in succession; in every matter newly established, expedients have mostly prevailed.

sentences.zh: 致使禮讓弗興，風俗未反。

translations.literal: This has caused ritual and deference not to arise and customs not to return to the good.
translations.idiomatic: This has caused ritual and deference not to arise and customs not to return to the good.

sentences.zh: 比年稍登稔，徭賦差輕，衣食不切，則教化可修矣。

translations.literal: In recent years harvests have been somewhat good, corvée and taxes somewhat lighter, and food and clothing no longer urgent—then moral transformation can be cultivated.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years harvests have been somewhat good, corvée and taxes somewhat lighter, and food and clothing no longer urgent—then moral transformation can be cultivated.

sentences.zh: 凡諸牧守令長，各宜洗心革意，上承朝旨，下宣教化矣。

translations.literal: All governors, magistrates, and chiefs should each cleanse the heart and reform the will, receiving the court's intent above and proclaiming moral transformation below.
translations.idiomatic: All governors, magistrates, and chiefs should each cleanse the heart and reform the will, receiving the court's intent above and proclaiming moral transformation below.

sentences.zh: 夫化者，貴能扇之以淳風，浸之乙太和，被之以道德，示之以樸素。

translations.literal: As for transformation, what is valued is the ability to fan people with pure customs, steep them in great harmony, clothe them in virtue and morality, and show them simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: As for transformation, what matters is the ability to fan people with pure customs, steep them in great harmony, clothe them in virtue and morality, and show them simplicity.

sentences.zh: 使百姓亹亹，日遷於善，邪偽之心，嗜欲之性，潛以消化，而不知其所以然，此之謂化也。

translations.literal: Make the common people diligent, moving day by day toward the good; perverse and false hearts and the nature of craving are quietly dissolved without their knowing why—this is called transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Make the common people diligent, moving day by day toward the good; perverse and false hearts and the nature of craving are quietly dissolved without their knowing why—this is called transformation.

sentences.zh: 然後教之以孝悌，使人慈愛；

translations.literal: Then teach them filial piety and brotherly duty to make people loving and kind;
translations.idiomatic: Then teach them filial piety and brotherly duty to make people loving and kind;

sentences.zh: 教之以仁順，使人和睦；

translations.literal: teach them benevolence and compliance to make people harmonious;
translations.idiomatic: teach them benevolence and compliance to make people harmonious;

sentences.zh: 教之以禮義，使人敬讓。

translations.literal: teach them ritual and righteousness to make people respectful and deferential.
translations.idiomatic: teach them ritual and righteousness to make people respectful and deferential.

sentences.zh: 慈愛則不遺其親，和睦則無怨於人，敬讓則不競於物。

translations.literal: With loving kindness one does not neglect one's kin; with harmony one bears no resentment toward others; with respect and deference one does not contend over things.
translations.idiomatic: With loving kindness one does not neglect one's kin; with harmony one bears no resentment toward others; with respect and deference one does not contend over things.

sentences.zh: 三者既備，則王道成矣。

translations.literal: When these three are complete, the kingly way is achieved.
translations.idiomatic: When these three are complete, the kingly way is achieved.

sentences.zh: 此之謂教也。

translations.literal: This is called instruction.
translations.idiomatic: This is called instruction.

sentences.zh: 先王之所以移風易俗，還淳反素，垂拱而臨天下以至於太平者，莫不由此。

translations.literal: The reason former kings were able to shift customs and change habits, return to purity and restore simplicity, and rule the realm in repose until reaching great peace—none failed to do so by this path.
translations.idiomatic: The reason former kings were able to shift customs and change habits, return to purity and restore simplicity, and rule the realm in repose until reaching great peace—none failed to do so by this path.

sentences.zh: 此之謂要道也。

translations.literal: This is called the essential way.
translations.idiomatic: This is called the essential way.

sentences.zh: 其三，盡地利，曰：

translations.literal: The third: fully employ the land's advantages. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The third edict, on fully employing the land's advantages, reads:

sentences.zh: 人生天地之間，衣食為命。

translations.literal: Human life between heaven and earth depends on food and clothing for its sustenance.
translations.idiomatic: Human life between heaven and earth depends on food and clothing for its sustenance.

sentences.zh: 食不足則饑，衣不足則寒。

translations.literal: Insufficient food brings hunger; insufficient clothing brings cold.
translations.idiomatic: Insufficient food brings hunger; insufficient clothing brings cold.

sentences.zh: 饑寒切體，而欲使人興行禮讓者，此猶逆阪走丸，勢不可得也。

translations.literal: When hunger and cold cut to the bone, yet one wishes to make people rise and practice ritual and deference, it is like rolling a ball uphill—the thing cannot be done.
translations.idiomatic: When hunger and cold cut to the bone, yet one wishes to make people rise and practice ritual and deference, it is like rolling a ball uphill—the thing cannot be done.

sentences.zh: 是以古之聖王知其若此，先足其衣食，然後教化隨之。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity, knowing this, first made food and clothing sufficient and only then let moral transformation follow.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage kings of antiquity, knowing this, first made food and clothing sufficient and only then let moral transformation follow.

sentences.zh: 夫衣食所以足者，由於地利盡。

translations.literal: The reason food and clothing can be sufficient is that the land's advantages are fully employed.
translations.idiomatic: The reason food and clothing can be sufficient is that the land's advantages are fully employed.

sentences.zh: 地利所以盡者，由於勸課有方。

translations.literal: The reason the land's advantages can be fully employed is that encouragement and supervision are properly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: The reason the land's advantages can be fully employed is that encouragement and supervision are properly ordered.

sentences.zh: 主此教者，在乎牧守令長而已。

translations.literal: Those who preside over this instruction are none other than governors and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: Those who preside over this instruction are none other than governors and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 人者冥也，智不自周，必待勸教然後得盡其力。

translations.literal: People are benighted; their intelligence does not extend everywhere by itself—they must wait for encouragement and instruction before they can fully exert their strength.
translations.idiomatic: People are benighted; their intelligence does not extend everywhere by itself—they must wait for encouragement and instruction before they can fully exert their strength.

sentences.zh: 諸州郡縣，每至歲首，必戎敕部人，無問少長，但能操持農器者，皆令就田，墾發以時，勿失其所。

translations.literal: In all prefectures, commanderies, and counties, at the start of each year they must sternly admonish the people: regardless of age, all who can handle farming tools are to be sent to the fields, opening and cultivating land in season without missing the proper time.
translations.idiomatic: In all prefectures, commanderies, and counties, at the start of each year they must sternly admonish the people: regardless of age, all who can handle farming tools are to be sent to the fields, opening and cultivating land in season without missing the proper time.

sentences.zh: 及布種既訖，嘉苗須理，麥秋在野，蠶停於室，若此之時，皆宜少長悉力，男女並功，若揚湯救火，寇盜之將至，然後可使農夫不失其業，蠶婦得就其功。

translations.literal: When sowing is finished, fine seedlings must be tended; when wheat ripens in the fields and silkworms rest in the chambers—at such times young and old alike should exert all strength, men and women working together as if skimming boiling water or fighting fire or robbers about to arrive; only then can farmers keep their livelihood and silk workers complete their work.
translations.idiomatic: When sowing is finished, fine seedlings must be tended; when wheat ripens in the fields and silkworms rest in the chambers—at such times young and old alike should exert all strength, men and women working together as if skimming boiling water, fighting fire, or facing robbers about to arrive; only then can farmers keep their livelihood and silk workers complete their work.

sentences.zh: 若遊手怠惰，早歸晚出，好逸惡勞，不勤事業者，則正長牒名郡縣，守令隨事加罰，罪一勸百。

translations.literal: If there are idlers who are lazy, leave early and return late, love ease and hate labor, and do not diligently pursue their work, the local chiefs are to register their names with the commandery and county, and governors and magistrates are to punish according to the offense—one punishment warning a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: If there are idlers who are lazy, leave early and return late, love ease and hate labor, and do not diligently pursue their work, the local chiefs are to register their names with the commandery and county, and governors and magistrates are to punish according to the offense—one punishment warning a hundred.

sentences.zh: 此則明宰之教也。

translations.literal: This is the instruction of a clear-sighted magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: This is the instruction of a clear-sighted magistrate.

sentences.zh: 夫百畝之田，必春耕之，夏種之，秋收之，然後冬食之。

translations.literal: A field of a hundred mu must be plowed in spring, sown in summer, and harvested in autumn before it can be eaten in winter.
translations.idiomatic: A field of a hundred mu must be plowed in spring, sown in summer, and harvested in autumn before it can be eaten in winter.

sentences.zh: 此三時者，農之要月也。

translations.literal: These three seasons are the crucial months of farming.
translations.idiomatic: These three seasons are the crucial months of farming.

sentences.zh: 若失其一時，則穀不可得而食。

translations.literal: If one of these seasons is missed, grain cannot be obtained for food.
translations.idiomatic: If one of these seasons is missed, grain cannot be obtained for food.

sentences.zh: 故先王之戒曰：「一夫不耕，天下必有受其饑者；

translations.literal: Therefore the warning of former kings says: "If one man does not plow, under heaven there must be someone who suffers hunger because of him;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the warning of former kings says: "If one man does not plow, under heaven there must be someone who suffers hunger because of him;

sentences.zh: 一婦不織，天下必有受其寒者。」

translations.literal: if one woman does not weave, under heaven there must be someone who suffers cold because of her.
translations.idiomatic: if one woman does not weave, under heaven there must be someone who suffers cold because of her.

sentences.zh: 若此三時，不務省事，而令人廢農者，是則絕人之命，驅以就死然。

translations.literal: If in these three seasons one does not attend to reducing burdens yet makes people abandon farming, this is cutting off people's lives and driving them toward death.
translations.idiomatic: If in these three seasons one does not attend to reducing burdens yet makes people abandon farming, this is cutting off people's lives and driving them toward death.

sentences.zh: 單劣之戶，及無牛之家，勸令有無相通，使得兼濟。

translations.literal: For weak and poor households and families without oxen, encourage those with resources and those without to help one another so that all may be mutually sustained.
translations.idiomatic: For weak and poor households and families without oxen, encourage those with resources and those without to help one another so that all may be mutually sustained.

sentences.zh: 三農之隙，及陰雨之暇，又當教人種桑植果，藝其蔬菜，修其園圃，畜育雞豚，以備生生之資，以供養老之具。

translations.literal: In the intervals between the three farming seasons and during rainy days, they should also teach people to plant mulberry and fruit trees, cultivate vegetables, tend gardens, and raise chickens and pigs to supply the means of livelihood and provide for old age.
translations.idiomatic: In the intervals between the three farming seasons and during rainy days, they should also teach people to plant mulberry and fruit trees, cultivate vegetables, tend gardens, and raise chickens and pigs to supply the means of livelihood and provide for old age.

sentences.zh: 夫為政不欲過辭，碎則人煩；

translations.literal: In governing one should not use excessive words; if too fragmented, people are troubled;
translations.idiomatic: In governing one should not use excessive words; if too fragmented, people are troubled;

sentences.zh: 勸課亦不容太簡，簡則人怠。

translations.literal: encouragement and supervision also cannot be too simple; if too simple, people grow slack.
translations.idiomatic: encouragement and supervision also cannot be too simple; if too simple, people grow slack.

sentences.zh: 善為政者，必消息時宜而適煩簡之中。

translations.literal: One who governs well must weigh the needs of the time and hit the balance between trouble and simplicity.
translations.idiomatic: One who governs well must weigh the needs of the time and hit the balance between trouble and simplicity.

sentences.zh: 故詩曰：「不剛不柔，布政優優，百祿是求。」

translations.literal: Therefore the Odes say: "Neither hard nor soft, spread governance with ease, and seek the hundred blessings.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Odes say: "Neither hard nor soft, spread governance with ease, and seek the hundred blessings.

sentences.zh: 如不能爾，則必陷於刑辟矣。

translations.literal: If one cannot do this, one will surely fall into punishment by law.
translations.idiomatic: If one cannot do this, one will surely fall under punishment by law.

sentences.zh: 其四，擢賢良，曰：

translations.literal: The fourth: promote the worthy and good. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The fourth edict, on promoting the worthy and good, reads:

sentences.zh: 天生蒸黎，不能自化，故必立君以理之。

translations.literal: Heaven born the multitude of the people; they cannot transform themselves, therefore a ruler must be established to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven born the multitude of the people; they cannot transform themselves, therefore a ruler must be established to govern them.

sentences.zh: 人君不能獨理，故必置臣以佐之。

translations.literal: A ruler cannot govern alone, therefore ministers must be appointed to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler cannot govern alone, therefore ministers must be appointed to assist him.

sentences.zh: 上自帝王，下及列國，置臣得賢則安，失賢則亂，此乃自然之理，百王不能易也。

translations.literal: From emperors above down to feudal states below, if worthy ministers are appointed there is peace; if worthy ministers are lost there is chaos—this is the natural principle, which no king of the hundred reigns can alter.
translations.idiomatic: From emperors above down to feudal states below, if worthy ministers are appointed there is peace; if worthy ministers are lost there is chaos—this is the natural principle, which no king of the hundred reigns can alter.

sentences.zh: 今刺史縣令，悉有僚吏，皆佐助之人也。

translations.literal: Today provincial inspectors and county magistrates all have staff officers— all are people who assist in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Today provincial inspectors and county magistrates all have staff officers—all are people who assist in governance.

sentences.zh: 刺史府官則命於天朝；

translations.literal: Officials of the inspector's office are appointed by the imperial court;
translations.idiomatic: Officials of the inspector's office are appointed by the imperial court;

sentences.zh: 其州吏以下，並牧守自置。

translations.literal: the clerks of the province and below are all appointed by governors themselves.
translations.idiomatic: the clerks of the province and below are all appointed by governors themselves.

sentences.zh: 自昔以來，州郡大夫，但取門資，多不擇賢良；

translations.literal: From old times provincial and commandery chiefs have taken only hereditary privilege and mostly not chosen the worthy and good;
translations.idiomatic: From old times provincial and commandery chiefs have taken only hereditary privilege and mostly not chosen the worthy and good;

sentences.zh: 末曹小吏，唯試刀筆，並不問志行。

translations.literal: petty clerks in lower offices have been tested only on brush and document skills and never asked about purpose and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: petty clerks in lower offices have been tested only on brush and document skills and never asked about purpose and conduct.

sentences.zh: 夫門資者，乃先世之爵祿，無妨子孫之愚瞽；

translations.literal: Hereditary privilege is the rank and emolument of former generations—it does not prevent descendants from being foolish and blind;
translations.idiomatic: Hereditary privilege is the rank and emolument of former generations—it does not prevent descendants from being foolish and blind;

sentences.zh: 刀筆者，乃身外之末材，不廢性行之澆偽。

translations.literal: brush and document skills are minor talents external to the person—they do not eliminate shallow falsity of character and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Brush and document skills are minor talents external to the person—they do not eliminate shallow falsity of character and conduct.

sentences.zh: 若門資之中而得賢良，是則策騏驥而取千里也；

translations.literal: If among those of hereditary privilege one finds the worthy and good, it is like putting a swift horse to the whip and taking a thousand li;
translations.idiomatic: If among those of hereditary privilege one finds the worthy and good, it is like putting a swift horse to the whip and taking a thousand li;

sentences.zh: 若門資之中而得愚瞽，是則土牛木馬，形似而用非，不可以涉道也。

translations.literal: If among those of hereditary privilege one finds the foolish and blind, it is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—similar in form but useless in function, unable to travel the road.
translations.idiomatic: If among those of hereditary privilege one finds the foolish and blind, it is like an earthen ox or wooden horse—similar in form but useless in function, unable to travel the road.

sentences.zh: 若刀筆之中而得志行，是則金相玉質，內外俱美，實為人寶也；

translations.literal: If among clerks one finds purpose and conduct, it is like gold in appearance and jade in substance—beautiful within and without, truly a treasure among men;
translations.idiomatic: If among clerks one finds purpose and conduct, it is like gold in appearance and jade in substance—beautiful within and without, truly a treasure among men;

sentences.zh: 若刀筆之中而得澆偽，是則飾畫朽木，悅目一時，不可以充榱椽之用也。

translations.literal: If among clerks one finds shallow falsity, it is like painting rotten wood—pleasing to the eye for a moment but unable to serve as rafters and beams.
translations.idiomatic: If among clerks one finds shallow falsity, it is like painting rotten wood—pleasing to the eye for a moment but unable to serve as rafters and beams.

sentences.zh: 今之選舉者，當不限資陰，唯在得人。

translations.literal: In selection and appointment today, one should not be limited by pedigree and background—what matters is obtaining the right people.
translations.idiomatic: In selection and appointment today, one should not be limited by pedigree and background—what matters is obtaining the right people.

sentences.zh: 苟得其人，自可起廝養而為卿相，則伊尹、傅說是也，而況兄州郡之職乎？

translations.literal: If one obtains the right person, one can raise him from stable hand to minister and chancellor—as with Yi Yin and Fu Yue—how much more for provincial and commandery posts?
translations.idiomatic: If one obtains the right person, one can raise him from stable hand to minister and chancellor—as with Yi Yin and Fu Yue—how much more for provincial and commandery posts?

sentences.zh: 苟非其人，則丹硃、商均雖帝王之胤，不能守百里之封，而況於公卿之胄乎？

translations.literal: If one does not obtain the right person, then Danzhu and Shangjun, though descendants of emperors, could not hold fiefs of a hundred li—how much less the offspring of dukes and ministers?
translations.idiomatic: If one does not obtain the right person, then Danzhu and Shangjun, though descendants of emperors, could not hold fiefs of a hundred li—how much less the offspring of dukes and ministers?

sentences.zh: 由此而言，官人之道可見矣。

translations.literal: From this it can be seen what the way of appointing officials is.
translations.idiomatic: From this one can see what the way of appointing officials requires.

sentences.zh: 凡所求材藝者，為其可以理人。

translations.literal: All talent and skill that are sought are sought because they can govern people.
translations.idiomatic: All talent and skill that are sought are sought because they can govern people.

sentences.zh: 若有材藝而以正直為本者，必以材而為理也；

translations.literal: If one has talent and skill with uprightness as the foundation, one will surely use that talent to govern;
translations.idiomatic: If one has talent and skill with uprightness as the foundation, one will surely use that talent to govern;

sentences.zh: 若有材藝而以奸偽為本者，將因其官而亂也，何致化之可得乎？

translations.literal: if one has talent and skill with treachery and falsity as the foundation, one will use one's office to bring chaos—how then can transformation be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: if one has talent and skill with treachery and falsity as the foundation, one will use one's office to bring chaos—how then can transformation be achieved?

sentences.zh: 是故將求材藝，必先擇志行，善者則舉之，其志行不善則去之。

translations.literal: Therefore in seeking talent and skill one must first choose purpose and conduct; the good are to be promoted, those whose purpose and conduct are not good are to be removed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in seeking talent and skill one must first choose purpose and conduct; promote the good and remove those whose purpose and conduct are not good.

sentences.zh: 而今擇人者，多雲邦國無賢，莫知所舉。

translations.literal: Yet those who select people today often say the state has no worthy men and do not know whom to recommend.
translations.idiomatic: Yet those who select people today often say the state has no worthy men and do not know whom to recommend.

sentences.zh: 此乃未之思也，非適理之論。

translations.literal: This is failure to think the matter through—not a reasonable argument.
translations.idiomatic: This is failure to think the matter through—not a reasonable argument.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，古人有言；

translations.literal: The reason is that the ancients had a saying:
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that the ancients had a saying:

sentences.zh: 明主聿興，不降佐於昊天；

translations.literal: When a clear-sighted lord rises, he does not summon assistants down from the vast heaven;
translations.idiomatic: When a clear-sighted lord rises, he does not summon assistants down from the vast heaven;

sentences.zh: 大人基命，不擢才於后土。

translations.literal: when a great man receives the mandate, he does not pluck talent up from the earth below.
translations.idiomatic: when a great man receives the mandate, he does not pluck talent up from the earth below.

sentences.zh: 常引一世之人，理一世之務。

translations.literal: He always draws on the people of his age to govern the affairs of his age.
translations.idiomatic: He always draws on the people of his age to govern the affairs of his age.

sentences.zh: 故殷、周不待稷、契之臣，魏、晉無假蕭、曹之佐。

translations.literal: Therefore Yin and Zhou did not wait for ministers like Ji and Qi; Wei and Jin had no need to borrow assistants like Xiao and Cao.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yin and Zhou did not wait for ministers like Ji and Qi; Wei and Jin had no need to borrow assistants like Xiao and Cao.

sentences.zh: 仲尼曰：「十室之邑，必有忠信如丘者焉。」

translations.literal: Confucius said: "In a settlement of ten households there must be someone as loyal and trustworthy as I am.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "In a settlement of ten households there must be someone as loyal and trustworthy as I am.

sentences.zh: 豈有萬家之都，而雲無士？

translations.literal: How can there be a city of ten thousand households yet people say there are no worthy men?
translations.idiomatic: How can there be a city of ten thousand households yet people say there are no worthy men?

sentences.zh: 但求之不勤，擇之不審，或授之不得其所，任之不盡其材，故云無耳。

translations.literal: It is only that the search is not diligent, the choice not careful, or appointment is not to the right place and employment does not use one's full talent—therefore they say there are none.
translations.idiomatic: It is only that the search is not diligent, the choice not careful, or appointment is not to the right place and employment does not use one's full talent—therefore they say there are none.

sentences.zh: 古人云：「千人之秀曰英，萬人之英曰俊。」

translations.literal: The ancients said: "The outstanding among a thousand are called heroes; the hero among ten thousand is called a paragon.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said: "The outstanding among a thousand are called heroes; the hero among ten thousand is called a paragon.

sentences.zh: 今之智效一官，行聞一邦者，豈非近英俊之士也？

translations.literal: Those today whose wisdom serves one office and whose conduct is known in one state—are they not nearly such outstanding men?
translations.idiomatic: Those today whose wisdom serves one office and whose conduct is known in one state—are they not nearly such outstanding men?

sentences.zh: 但能勤而審之，去虛取實，各得州郡之最而用之，則人無多少，皆足化矣。

translations.literal: If one can only be diligent and careful, discard the empty and take the solid, and employ the best each province and commandery has to offer, then regardless of numbers all will suffice for transformation.
translations.idiomatic: If one can only be diligent and careful, discard the empty and take the solid, and employ the best each province and commandery has to offer, then regardless of numbers all will suffice for transformation.

sentences.zh: 孰云無賢！

translations.literal: Who can say there are no worthy men!
translations.idiomatic: Who can say there are no worthy men!

sentences.zh: 夫良玉未剖，與瓦石相類；

translations.literal: Fine jade before it is cut resembles tile and stone;
translations.idiomatic: Fine jade before it is cut resembles tile and stone;

sentences.zh: 名驥未馳，與駑馬相雜。

translations.literal: a famed swift horse before it runs is mixed with draft nags.
translations.idiomatic: a famed swift horse before it runs is mixed with draft nags.

sentences.zh: 及其剖而瑩之，馳而試之，玉石駑驥，然後始分。

translations.literal: Only when it is cut and polished, run and tested, are jade and stone, nag and swift horse, finally distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Only when it is cut and polished, run and tested, are jade and stone, nag and swift horse, finally distinguished.

sentences.zh: 彼賢士之未用也，混於凡品，竟何以異。

translations.literal: When worthy men are not yet employed, they are mixed among ordinary ranks—how in the end can one tell the difference?
translations.idiomatic: When worthy men are not yet employed, they are mixed among ordinary ranks—how in the end can one tell the difference?

sentences.zh: 要任之以事業，責之以成務，方與彼庸流較然不同。

translations.literal: The point is to entrust them with undertakings and charge them with completing tasks—only then are they clearly different from the mediocre crowd.
translations.idiomatic: The point is to entrust them with undertakings and charge them with completing tasks—only then are they clearly different from the mediocre crowd.

sentences.zh: 或呂望之屠釣，百里奚之飯牛，寧生之扣角，管夷吾之三敗，當此之時，悠悠之徒，豈謂其賢？

translations.literal: Whether Lü Wang butchering and fishing, Baili Xi feeding cattle, Ning Sheng striking his horns, or Guan Yiwu suffering three defeats—at such times, would the idle masses have called them worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Whether Lü Wang butchering and fishing, Baili Xi feeding cattle, Ning Sheng striking his horns, or Guan Yiwu suffering three defeats—at such times, would the idle masses have called them worthy?

sentences.zh: 及升王朝，登霸國，積數十年，功成事立，始識其奇士也。

translations.literal: Only when they rose to the royal court, established hegemony, accumulated decades, and achievement and enterprise were complete did people first recognize them as extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Only when they rose to the royal court, established hegemony, accumulated decades, and achievement and enterprise were complete did people first recognize them as extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 於是後世稱之，不容於口。

translations.literal: Then later ages praised them—their names would not stay out of people's mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Then later ages praised them—their names would not stay out of people's mouths.

sentences.zh: 彼環瑋之才，不世之傑，尚不能以未遇之時，自異於凡品，況降此者哉！

translations.literal: Those talents of finest jade, heroes not of every age—even they could not distinguish themselves from ordinary ranks before they were discovered; how much less those below them!
translations.idiomatic: Those talents of finest jade, heroes not of every age—even they could not distinguish themselves from ordinary ranks before they were discovered; how much less those below them!

sentences.zh: 若必待太公而後用，是千載無太公；

translations.literal: If one must wait for Taigong before employing anyone, there would be no Taigong for a thousand years;
translations.idiomatic: If one must wait for Taigong before employing anyone, there would be no Taigong for a thousand years;

sentences.zh: 必待夷吾而後任，是百世無夷吾。

translations.literal: if one must wait for Yiwu before entrusting office, there would be no Yiwu for a hundred generations.
translations.idiomatic: if one must wait for Yiwu before entrusting office, there would be no Yiwu for a hundred generations.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，士必從微而至著，功必積小以至大，豈有未任而已成，不用而先達也？

translations.literal: The reason is that scholars must go from obscurity to prominence and achievement must accumulate from small to great—how could there be accomplishment before appointment or advancement before use?
translations.idiomatic: The reason is that scholars must go from obscurity to prominence and achievement must accumulate from small to great—how could there be accomplishment before appointment or advancement before use?

sentences.zh: 若識此理，則賢可求，士可擇。

translations.literal: If one understands this principle, the worthy can be sought and scholars can be chosen.
translations.idiomatic: If one understands this principle, the worthy can be sought and scholars can be chosen.

sentences.zh: 得賢而任之，得士而使之，則天下之理，何向而不可成也？

translations.literal: Obtain the worthy and employ them, obtain scholars and use them—then what principle under heaven could fail to be achieved?
translations.idiomatic: Obtain the worthy and employ them, obtain scholars and use them—then what principle under heaven could fail to be achieved?

sentences.zh: 然善官人者，必先省其官。

translations.literal: Yet one who is good at appointing officials must first reduce the number of offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one who is good at appointing officials must first reduce the number of offices.

sentences.zh: 官省，則善人易充。

translations.literal: When offices are reduced, good men are easily supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When offices are reduced, good men are easily supplied.

sentences.zh: 善人易充，則事無不理。

translations.literal: When good men are easily supplied, no affair goes ungoverned.
translations.idiomatic: When good men are easily supplied, no affair goes ungoverned.

sentences.zh: 官煩，則必雜不善之人。

translations.literal: When offices are numerous, unworthy people must be mixed in.
translations.idiomatic: When offices are numerous, unworthy people must be mixed in.

sentences.zh: 雜不善之人，則政必有得失。

translations.literal: When unworthy people are mixed in, governance must have gains and losses.
translations.idiomatic: When unworthy people are mixed in, governance must have gains and losses.

sentences.zh: 故語曰：「官省則事省，事省則人清；

translations.literal: Therefore a saying goes: "When offices are reduced, affairs are reduced; when affairs are reduced, people are clear;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a saying goes: "When offices are reduced, affairs are reduced; when affairs are reduced, people are clear;

sentences.zh: 官煩則事煩，事煩則人濁。」

translations.literal: when offices are numerous, affairs are numerous; when affairs are numerous, people are turbid.
translations.idiomatic: when offices are numerous, affairs are numerous; when affairs are numerous, people are turbid.

sentences.zh: 清濁之由，在於官之煩省。

translations.literal: The source of clarity and turbidity lies in whether offices are numerous or reduced.
translations.idiomatic: The source of clarity and turbidity lies in whether offices are numerous or reduced.

sentences.zh: 案今吏員，其數不少。

translations.literal: Consider the clerks and officials today—their number is not small.
translations.idiomatic: Consider the clerks and officials today—their number is not small.

sentences.zh: 昔人殷事廣，尚能克濟，況今戶口減耗？

translations.literal: In former times when population was dense and affairs broad, they could still manage—how much more now when households and population have declined?
translations.idiomatic: In former times when population was dense and affairs broad, they could still manage—how much more now when households and population have declined?

sentences.zh: 依員而置，猶以為少。

translations.literal: Even when offices are filled according to quota, they are still thought too few.
translations.idiomatic: Even when offices are filled according to quota, they are still thought too few.

sentences.zh: 如聞在下州郡，尚有兼假，擾亂細人，甚為無理。

translations.literal: It is heard that in lower provinces and commanderies there are still concurrent and acting appointments, disturbing common people—most unreasonable.
translations.idiomatic: It is heard that in lower provinces and commanderies there are still concurrent and acting appointments, disturbing common people—most unreasonable.

sentences.zh: 諸如此輩，悉宜罷黜，無得習常。

translations.literal: All such cases should be dismissed and removed; one must not treat this as customary.
translations.idiomatic: All such cases should be dismissed and removed; one must not treat this as customary.

sentences.zh: 非直州郡之官，宜須善人，爰至黨族閭里正長之職，皆當審擇，各得一鄉之選，以相監統。

translations.literal: Not only provincial and commandery officials need good men—even down to the chiefs of clans, neighborhoods, and hamlets, all should be carefully chosen, each obtaining the best choice of one village, to supervise and oversee one another.
translations.idiomatic: Not only provincial and commandery officials need good men—even down to the chiefs of clans, neighborhoods, and hamlets, all should be carefully chosen, each the best choice of one village, to supervise and oversee one another.

sentences.zh: 夫正長者，理人之基。

translations.literal: Local chiefs are the foundation of governing people.
translations.idiomatic: Local chiefs are the foundation of governing people.

sentences.zh: 基不傾者上必安。

translations.literal: If the foundation does not tilt, what is above must be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If the foundation does not tilt, what is above must be secure.

sentences.zh: 凡求賢之路，自非一途。

translations.literal: The paths of seeking the worthy are not of one kind alone.
translations.idiomatic: The paths of seeking the worthy are not of one kind alone.

sentences.zh: 然所以得之審者，必由任而試之，考而察之。

translations.literal: Yet the reason one can obtain them with certainty is that one must employ and test them, examine and inspect them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the reason one can obtain them with certainty is that one must employ and test them, examine and inspect them.

sentences.zh: 起于居家，至於鄉黨，訪其所以，觀其所由，則人道明矣，賢與不肖別矣。

translations.literal: From home life to village and neighborhood, inquire into the reasons and observe the sources—then the way of humanity is clear and the worthy and unworthy are distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: From home life to village and neighborhood, inquire into the reasons and observe the sources—then the way of humanity is clear and the worthy and unworthy are distinguished.

sentences.zh: 率此以求，則庶無愆悔矣。

translations.literal: Follow this in seeking and one will mostly avoid error and regret.
translations.idiomatic: Follow this in seeking and one will mostly avoid error and regret.

sentences.zh: 其五，恤獄訟，曰：

translations.literal: The fifth: care for prisons and litigation. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The fifth edict, on caring for prisons and litigation, reads:

sentences.zh: 人受陰陽之氣以生，有情有性。

translations.literal: People receive the qi of yin and yang to be born; they have feeling and nature.
translations.idiomatic: People receive the qi of yin and yang to be born; they have feeling and nature.

sentences.zh: 性則為善，情則為惡。

translations.literal: Nature tends toward good; feeling tends toward evil.
translations.idiomatic: Nature tends toward good; feeling tends toward evil.

sentences.zh: 善惡既分，賞罰隨焉。

translations.literal: Once good and evil are distinguished, reward and punishment follow.
translations.idiomatic: Once good and evil are distinguished, reward and punishment follow.

sentences.zh: 賞罰得中，則惡止而善勸；

translations.literal: When reward and punishment hit the mark, evil stops and good is encouraged;
translations.idiomatic: When reward and punishment hit the mark, evil stops and good is encouraged;

sentences.zh: 賞罰不中，則人無所措手足，則怨叛之心生。

translations.literal: when reward and punishment miss the mark, people do not know where to put hands or feet, and hearts of resentment and rebellion arise.
translations.idiomatic: when reward and punishment miss the mark, people do not know where to put hands or feet, and hearts of resentment and rebellion arise.

sentences.zh: 是以先王重之，特加戒慎者，欲使察獄之官，精心悉意，推究根源。

translations.literal: Therefore former kings weighted it heavily and added special caution, wishing that officials who examine prisons would concentrate their hearts and exhaust their intent, tracing matters to their roots.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore former kings weighted it heavily and added special caution, wishing that officials who examine prisons would concentrate their hearts and exhaust their intent, tracing matters to their roots.

sentences.zh: 先之以五聽，參之以證驗。

translations.literal: First apply the five modes of hearing, then cross-check with evidence and verification.
translations.idiomatic: First apply the five modes of hearing, then cross-check with evidence and verification.

sentences.zh: 妙睹情狀，窮鑒陷伏，使奸無所容，罪人必得。

translations.literal: Perceive the circumstances of feeling with subtlety, exhaustively discern hidden traps, leave no room for treachery, and ensure the guilty are caught.
translations.idiomatic: Perceive the circumstances of feeling with subtlety, exhaustively discern hidden traps, leave no room for treachery, and ensure the guilty are caught.

sentences.zh: 然後隨事加刑，輕重皆當，舍過矜愚，得情勿喜。

translations.literal: Then apply punishment according to the case, with light and heavy all appropriate; overlook minor faults and pity the foolish; when the truth is obtained, do not rejoice.
translations.idiomatic: Then apply punishment according to the case, with light and heavy all appropriate; overlook minor faults and pity the foolish; when the truth is obtained, do not rejoice.

sentences.zh: 又能消息情理，斟酌禮律，無不曲盡人心，而遠明大教，使獲罪者如歸。

translations.literal: One can also weigh feeling and principle, balance ritual and law, exhaust every turn of the human heart, and from afar illuminate great teaching, making those who receive punishment feel as if returning home.
translations.idiomatic: One can also weigh feeling and principle, balance ritual and law, exhaust every turn of the human heart, and from afar illuminate great teaching, making those who receive punishment feel as if returning home.

sentences.zh: 此則善之上者也。

translations.literal: This is the highest level of goodness.
translations.idiomatic: This is the highest level of goodness.

sentences.zh: 然宰守非一，不可人人皆有通識，推理求情，時或難盡。
