translations.literal: Yet governors and magistrates are not one person; not everyone can have comprehensive understanding, and reasoning to seek the truth of feeling is sometimes hard to complete.
translations.idiomatic: Yet governors and magistrates are not one person; not everyone can have comprehensive understanding, and reasoning to seek the truth of feeling is sometimes hard to complete.

sentences.zh: 唯當率至公之心，去阿枉之志，務求曲直，念盡平當。

translations.literal: One should only lead with a heart of utmost fairness, discard partial and crooked intent, strive to seek right and wrong, and think through to full equity.
translations.idiomatic: One should only lead with a heart of utmost fairness, discard partial and crooked intent, strive to seek right and wrong, and think through to full equity.

sentences.zh: 聽察之理，必窮所見，然後拷訊以法，不苛不暴，有疑則從輕，未審不妄罰，隨事斷理，獄無停滯。

translations.literal: In the principle of hearing and examining, one must exhaust what is seen; then interrogate by law, neither harsh nor violent; when in doubt lean toward leniency; when not yet clear do not punish rashly; decide each case on its merits and let prisons have no backlog.
translations.idiomatic: In the principle of hearing and examining, one must exhaust what is seen; then interrogate by law, neither harsh nor violent; when in doubt lean toward leniency; when not yet clear do not punish rashly; decide each case on its merits and let prisons have no backlog.

sentences.zh: 此亦其次。

translations.literal: This is also acceptable—the second rank.
translations.idiomatic: This is also acceptable—the second rank.

sentences.zh: 若乃不仁恕而肆其殘暴，同人木石，專用捶楚。

translations.literal: If one is not benevolent and forgiving but indulges cruelty, treating people like wood and stone and relying solely on beating and flogging.
translations.idiomatic: If one is not benevolent and forgiving but indulges cruelty, treating people like wood and stone and relying solely on beating and flogging.

sentences.zh: 巧詐者，雖事彰而獲免；

translations.literal: the cunning and deceitful, though their deeds are exposed, may escape;
translations.idiomatic: the cunning and deceitful, though their deeds are exposed, may escape;

sentences.zh: 辭弱者，乃無罪而被罰。

translations.literal: the weak in speech may be punished though innocent.
translations.idiomatic: the weak in speech may be punished though innocent.

sentences.zh: 有如此者，斯則下矣，非共理所寄。

translations.literal: If there are such cases, this is the lowest rank—not what joint governance should rely on.
translations.idiomatic: If there are such cases, this is the lowest rank—not what joint governance should rely on.

sentences.zh: 今之宰守，當勤於中科，而慕其上善。

translations.literal: Governors and magistrates today should strive for the middle rank and aspire to the highest goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Governors and magistrates today should strive for the middle rank and aspire to the highest goodness.

sentences.zh: 如在下條，則刑所不赦。

translations.literal: If they fall into the lowest rank, punishment will not pardon them.
translations.idiomatic: If they fall into the lowest rank, punishment will not pardon them.

sentences.zh: 又當深思遠大，念存德教。

translations.literal: They should also think deeply and far, keeping moral teaching in mind.
translations.idiomatic: They should also think deeply and far, keeping moral teaching in mind.

sentences.zh: 先王之制曰：與殺無辜，寧赦有罪；

translations.literal: The regulation of former kings says: Better to pardon the guilty than to kill the innocent;
translations.idiomatic: The regulation of former kings says: Better to pardon the guilty than to kill the innocent;

sentences.zh: 與其害善，寧其利淫。

translations.literal: better to let the licentious benefit than to harm the good.
translations.idiomatic: better to let the licentious benefit than to harm the good.

sentences.zh: 明必不得中，寧濫舍有罪，不謬害善人也。

translations.literal: If one clearly cannot hit the mark, better to pardon the guilty too broadly than to wrongly harm good people.
translations.idiomatic: If one clearly cannot hit the mark, better to pardon the guilty too broadly than to wrongly harm good people.

sentences.zh: 今之從政者則不然，深文巧劾，甯致善人于法，不免有罪于刑。

translations.literal: Those in government today are not so; they deepen the letter of the law and craft accusations, preferring to bring good people under the law rather than fail to punish the guilty.
translations.idiomatic: Those in government today are not so; they deepen the letter of the law and craft accusations, preferring to bring good people under the law rather than fail to punish the guilty.

sentences.zh: 所以然者，非皆好殺人也，但雲為吏寧酷，可免後患。

translations.literal: The reason is not that all love killing; they only say that as officials it is better to be harsh, so later troubles can be avoided.
translations.idiomatic: The reason is not that all love killing; they only say that as officials it is better to be harsh, so later troubles can be avoided.

sentences.zh: 此則情存自便，不念至公，奉法如此，皆奸人也。

translations.literal: This is keeping self-convenience in mind and not thinking of utmost fairness; those who uphold the law in this way are all wicked men.
translations.idiomatic: This is keeping self-convenience in mind and not thinking of utmost fairness; those who uphold the law in this way are all wicked men.

sentences.zh: 夫人者，天地之貴物，一死不可復生。

translations.literal: Human beings are the noble creatures of heaven and earth; once dead they cannot live again.
translations.idiomatic: Human beings are the noble creatures of heaven and earth; once dead they cannot live again.

sentences.zh: 然楚毒之下，以痛自誣，不被申理，遂陷刑戮者，將恐往往而有。

translations.literal: Yet under cruel torture, people falsely confess from pain, are not given a fair hearing, and fall into execution—I fear such cases are often found.
translations.idiomatic: Yet under cruel torture, people falsely confess from pain, are not given a fair hearing, and fall into execution—I fear such cases are often found.

sentences.zh: 是以自古已來，設五聽三宥之法，著明慎庶獄之典，此皆愛人甚也。

translations.literal: Therefore from antiquity the methods of the five hearings and three pardons were established and the canon of careful handling of common litigation was set forth—all because of great love for people.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore from antiquity the methods of the five hearings and three pardons were established and the canon of careful handling of common litigation was set forth—all because of great love for people.

sentences.zh: 凡伐木殺草，田獵不順，尚違時令而虧帝道；

translations.literal: Even felling trees, killing grass, or hunting out of season still violates the seasons and damages the imperial way;
translations.idiomatic: Even felling trees, killing grass, or hunting out of season still violates the seasons and damages the imperial way;

sentences.zh: 況刑罰不中，濫害善人，甯不傷天心，犯和氣！

translations.literal: how much more when punishments miss the mark and good people are harmed at random—will this not wound the heart of heaven and violate harmonious qi!
translations.idiomatic: how much more when punishments miss the mark and good people are harmed at random—will this not wound the heart of heaven and violate harmonious qi!

sentences.zh: 和氣損而欲陰陽調適，四時順育，萬物阜安，蒼生悅樂者，不可得也。

translations.literal: When harmonious qi is damaged yet one wishes yin and yang to be balanced, the four seasons to nurture in order, all things to flourish in peace, and the common people to rejoice—this cannot be obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When harmonious qi is damaged yet one wishes yin and yang to be balanced, the four seasons to nurture in order, all things to flourish in peace, and the common people to rejoice—this cannot be obtained.

sentences.zh: 故語曰，一夫籲嗟，王道為之傾覆，正謂此也。

translations.literal: Therefore a saying goes: One man's sigh can overturn the kingly way—this is exactly what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a saying goes: One man's sigh can overturn the kingly way—this is exactly what is meant.

sentences.zh: 凡百宰守，可無慎乎！

translations.literal: All governors and magistrates—can they fail to be careful!
translations.idiomatic: All governors and magistrates—can they fail to be careful!

sentences.zh: 若深奸巨猾，傷化敗俗，悖亂人倫，不忠不孝，故為背道，殺一利百，以清王化，重刑可也。

translations.literal: For deep treachery and great cunning that injure transformation and ruin customs, violate human relations, show disloyalty and unfilial conduct, and deliberately turn against the Way—if killing one benefits a hundred and clears kingly transformation, heavy punishment is permissible.
translations.idiomatic: For deep treachery and great cunning that injure transformation and ruin customs, violate human relations, show disloyalty and unfilial conduct, and deliberately turn against the Way—if killing one benefits a hundred and clears kingly transformation, heavy punishment is permissible.

sentences.zh: 識此二途，則刑政盡矣。

translations.literal: Understand these two paths and penal governance is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Understand these two paths and penal governance is complete.

sentences.zh: 其六，均賦役，曰：

translations.literal: The sixth: equalize levies and corvée. It says:
translations.idiomatic: The sixth edict, on equalizing levies and corvée, reads:

sentences.zh: 聖人之大寶曰位。

translations.literal: The great treasure of the sage is position.
translations.idiomatic: The great treasure of the sage is position.

sentences.zh: 何以位，曰仁。

translations.literal: How to hold position? Through benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: How to hold position? Through benevolence.

sentences.zh: 何以聚人，曰財。

translations.literal: How to gather people? Through wealth.
translations.idiomatic: How to gather people? Through wealth.

sentences.zh: 明先王必以財聚人，以仁也。

translations.literal: Clearly the former kings had to use wealth to gather people—through benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Clearly the former kings used wealth to gather people through benevolence.

sentences.zh: 今寇逆未平，軍國費廣，雖未遑減省，以恤人瘼，然宜令平均，使下無怨。

translations.literal: Today rebellion is not yet pacified and military and state expenses are vast; though there is not yet leisure to reduce and cut burdens to relieve people's distress, levies should still be made equal so those below have no grievance.
translations.idiomatic: Today rebellion is not yet pacified and military and state expenses are vast; though there is not yet leisure to reduce and cut burdens to relieve people's distress, levies should still be made equal so those below have no grievance.

sentences.zh: 平均者，不舍豪強而征貧弱，不縱奸巧而困愚拙，此之謂均也。

translations.literal: To equalize means not sparing the powerful while taxing the weak and poor, not indulging the cunning while trapping the foolish and clumsy—this is called fairness.
translations.idiomatic: To equalize means not sparing the powerful while taxing the weak and poor, not indulging the cunning while trapping the foolish and clumsy—this is called fairness.

sentences.zh: 故聖人曰：「蓋均無貧。」

translations.literal: Therefore the sage said: "When levies are equal, there is no poverty."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage said: "When levies are equal, there is no poverty."

sentences.zh: 然財貨之生，其功不易。

translations.literal: Yet the production of wealth and goods is not easily achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Yet producing wealth and goods is no easy task.

sentences.zh: 紡紝織績，起於有漸，非旬日之間，所可造次。

translations.literal: Spinning, reeling, weaving, and stitching begin gradually—they cannot be rushed in a matter of days.
translations.idiomatic: Spinning, reeling, weaving, and stitching build up gradually—they cannot be rushed in a matter of days.

sentences.zh: 必須勸課，使預營理。

translations.literal: Encouragement and supervision are required so that people prepare in advance.
translations.idiomatic: Encouragement and supervision are required so that people prepare in advance.

sentences.zh: 絹鄉先事織紝，麻土早修紡績。

translations.literal: In silk districts they should first attend to reeling and weaving; in hemp districts they should early prepare spinning and stitching.
translations.idiomatic: In silk districts they should first attend to reeling and weaving; in hemp districts they should early prepare spinning and stitching.

sentences.zh: 先時而備，至時而輸，故王賦獲供，下人無困。

translations.literal: Prepare ahead of time and deliver when due—then royal levies are supplied and the people below are not distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Prepare ahead of time and deliver when due—then royal levies are supplied and the common people are not distressed.

sentences.zh: 如其不預勸戒，臨時迫切，復恐稽緩，以為己過，捶撲交至，取辦目前。

translations.literal: If advance encouragement is not given and at the last moment urgency presses, fearing delay they take it as their own fault—beatings arrive in succession and they must produce results on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: If advance encouragement is not given and at the last moment urgency presses, fearing delay they take it as their own fault—beatings arrive in succession and they must produce results on the spot.

sentences.zh: 富商大賈，緣茲射利，有者從之貴買，無者與之舉息。

translations.literal: Great merchants and traders seize this chance for profit; those with goods sell at high prices, those without borrow at interest.
translations.idiomatic: Great merchants and traders seize this chance for profit; those with goods sell at high prices, those without borrow at interest.

sentences.zh: 輸稅之人，於是弊矣。

translations.literal: Those who pay taxes are thereby ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Those who pay taxes are thereby ruined.

sentences.zh: 租稅之時，雖有大式，至於斟酌貧富，差次先後，皆事起於正長，而系之於守令。

translations.literal: At tax time, though there is a great standard, weighing rich and poor and ordering priority and sequence all begin with local chiefs and depend on governors and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: At tax time, though there is a great standard, weighing rich and poor and ordering priority and sequence all begin with local chiefs and depend on governors and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 若斟酌得所，則政和而人悅；

translations.literal: If the weighing is appropriate, governance is harmonious and people are pleased;
translations.idiomatic: If the weighing is appropriate, governance is harmonious and people are pleased;

sentences.zh: 若檢理無方，則吏奸而人怨。

translations.literal: if inspection and management lack method, officials grow wicked and people resent.
translations.idiomatic: if inspection and management lack method, officials grow wicked and people resent.

sentences.zh: 又差發徭役，多不存意，致令貧弱者或重徭而遠戍，富強者或輕使而近防。

translations.literal: In assigning corvée and service as well, many show no care, so the weak and poor may bear heavy corvée and garrison far away while the rich and strong may receive light duty and guard nearby.
translations.idiomatic: In assigning corvée and service as well, many show no care, so the weak and poor may bear heavy corvée and garrison far away while the rich and strong may receive light duty and guard nearby.

sentences.zh: 守令用懷如此，不存恤人之心，皆王政之罪人也。

translations.literal: When governors and magistrates hold such intent and keep no heart to care for people, all are criminals against kingly governance.
translations.idiomatic: When governors and magistrates hold such intent and keep no heart to care for people, all are criminals against kingly governance.

sentences.zh: 周文甚重之，常置諸坐右。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued them greatly and always kept them at his right hand.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued them greatly and always kept them at his right hand.

sentences.zh: 又令百司習誦之，其牧守令長非通六條及計帳者，不得居官。

translations.literal: He also ordered the hundred offices to study and recite them; governors, magistrates, and chiefs who did not master the Six Edicts and ledger accounts could not hold office.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered the hundred offices to study and recite them; governors, magistrates, and chiefs who did not master the Six Edicts and ledger accounts could not hold office.

sentences.zh: 自有晉之季，文章競為浮華，遂以成俗。

translations.literal: From the late Jin onward, writing competed in ornate extravagance until it became custom.
translations.idiomatic: From the late Jin onward, writing competed in ornate extravagance until it became custom.

sentences.zh: 周文欲革其弊，因魏帝祭廟，群臣畢至，乃命綽為大誥，奏行之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to reform this abuse; when the Wei emperor sacrificed at the ancestral temple and all ministers assembled, he ordered Chuo to draft the Great Proclamation and memorialized the throne to put it into effect.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou wished to reform this abuse; when the Wei emperor sacrificed at the ancestral temple and all ministers assembled, he ordered Chuo to draft the Great Proclamation and submitted it for implementation.

sentences.zh: 其詞曰：

translations.literal: Its words say:
translations.idiomatic: It reads:

sentences.zh: 惟中興十有一年仲夏，庶邦百辟，咸會于王庭。

translations.literal: In the midsummer of the eleventh year of the Restoration, the myriad states and hundred ministers all assembled at the royal court.
translations.idiomatic: In the midsummer of the eleventh year of the Restoration, the myriad states and hundred ministers all assembled at the royal court.

sentences.zh: 柱國泰洎群公列將罔不來朝。

translations.literal: The Pillar of State Tai and the dukes and generals—none failed to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: The Pillar of State Tai and the dukes and generals—none failed to come to court.

sentences.zh: 時乃大稽百憲，敷於庶邦，用綏我王度。

translations.literal: Then the hundred statutes were broadly examined and proclaimed to the myriad states, to settle our royal measure.
translations.idiomatic: Then the hundred statutes were broadly examined and proclaimed to the myriad states, to settle our royal measure.

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「或堯命羲和，允厘百工。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Of old Yao appointed Xi and He and truly ordered the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Of old Yao appointed Xi and He and truly ordered the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 舜命九官，庶績咸熙。

translations.literal: Shun appointed the nine ministers and all achievements flourished.
translations.idiomatic: Shun appointed the nine ministers and all achievements flourished.

sentences.zh: 武丁命說，克號高宗。

translations.literal: Wuding appointed Yue and was able to be called High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: Wuding appointed Yue and was able to be called High Ancestor.

sentences.zh: 時惟休哉，朕其欽若。

translations.literal: How fine was that age—I shall reverently follow it.
translations.idiomatic: How fine was that age—I shall reverently follow it.

sentences.zh: 格爾有位，胥暨我太祖之庭，朕將丕命女以厥官。」

translations.literal: Come, you who hold office, all to the court of our Grand Ancestor—I shall greatly charge you with your posts."
translations.idiomatic: Come, you who hold office, all to the court of our Grand Ancestor—I shall greatly charge you with your posts."

sentences.zh: 六月丁巳，皇帝朝格于太廟，凡厥具僚，罔不在位。

translations.literal: On the ding-si day of the sixth month the emperor at dawn arrived at the Grand Temple; all the assembled officials—none was not in place.
translations.idiomatic: On the ding-si day of the sixth month the emperor at dawn arrived at the Grand Temple; all the assembled officials—none was not in place.

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「咨我元輔、群公、列將、百辟、卿士、庶尹、禦事，朕惟夤敷祖宗之靈命，稽于先王之典訓，以大誥於爾在位。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Consult, my chief minister, dukes, generals, hundred ministers, officers, various directors, and attendants—I have reverently received the numinous mandate of the ancestors, examined the canon and instruction of former kings, and with this Great Proclamation address you who hold office.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Consult, my chief minister, dukes, generals, hundred ministers, officers, various directors, and attendants—I have reverently received the numinous mandate of the ancestors, examined the canon and instruction of former kings, and with this Great Proclamation address you who hold office.

sentences.zh: 昔我太祖神皇，肇膺明命，以創我皇基。

translations.literal: Formerly our Grand Ancestor the Divine Emperor first received the bright mandate and founded our imperial foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly our Grand Ancestor the Divine Emperor first received the bright mandate and founded our imperial foundation.

sentences.zh: 烈祖、景宗，廓開四表，底定武功。

translations.literal: Our Resolute Ancestor and Illustrious Ancestor broadened the four quarters and settled military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Our Resolute Ancestor and Illustrious Ancestor broadened the four quarters and settled military achievement.

sentences.zh: 暨乎文祖，誕敷文德。

translations.literal: When it came to our Literary Ancestor, he greatly spread civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When it came to our Literary Ancestor, he greatly spread civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 龔惟武考，不霣其舊。

translations.literal: Respectfully our Martial Father did not let the old ways fall away.
translations.idiomatic: Respectfully our Martial Father did not let the old ways fall away.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，陵夷之弊，用興大難於彼東土，則我黎庶，咸墜塗炭。

translations.literal: From that time onward decline and decay arose; great calamity rose in that eastern land and our common people all fell into fire and charcoal.
translations.idiomatic: From that time onward decline and decay arose; great calamity rose in that eastern land and our common people all fell into fire and charcoal.

sentences.zh: 惟台一人，纘戎下武，夙夜祗畏，若涉大川，罔識攸濟。

translations.literal: I alone, inheriting the martial task and following the martial way, day and night revere in fear as if crossing a great river—I know not where to cross.
translations.idiomatic: I alone, inheriting the martial task and following the martial way, day and night revere in fear as if crossing a great river—I know not where to cross.

sentences.zh: 是用稽於帝典，揆于王度，拯我人瘼。

translations.literal: Therefore I examine the canon of the emperors, measure against the royal measure, and rescue our people's distress.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I examine the canon of the emperors, measure against the royal measure, and rescue our people's distress.

sentences.zh: 惟彼哲王，示我通訓，曰天生黎蒸，罔克自乂，上帝降鑒叡聖，植元後以乂之。

translations.literal: Those wise kings showed me the thorough instruction, saying: Heaven born the multitude—they cannot govern themselves; High God sent down insight to the wise and sage and established the chief ruler to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Those wise kings showed me the thorough instruction, saying: Heaven born the multitude—they cannot govern themselves; High God sent down insight to the wise and sage and established the chief ruler to govern them.

sentences.zh: 時惟元後弗克獨乂，博求明德，命百辟群吏以佐之。

translations.literal: When the chief ruler could not govern alone, he broadly sought the bright and virtuous and appointed the hundred ministers and host of officials to assist him.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief ruler could not govern alone, he broadly sought the bright and virtuous and appointed the hundred ministers and host of officials to assist him.

sentences.zh: 肆天之命辟，辟之命這，惟以恤人，弗惟逸豫。

translations.literal: Thus Heaven charges the ruler; the ruler charges his ministers—only to care for the people, not for ease and pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Heaven charges the ruler; the ruler charges his ministers—only to care for the people, not for ease and pleasure.

sentences.zh: 辟惟元首，庶黎惟趾，股肱惟弼。

translations.literal: The ruler is the head, the multitude the feet, the arms and legs the assistants.
translations.idiomatic: The ruler is the head, the multitude the feet, the arms and legs the assistants.

sentences.zh: 上下一體，各勤攸司，茲用克臻於皇極。

translations.literal: Above and below are one body; each diligently performs his duty—by this one can reach the royal pinnacle.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below are one body; each diligently performs his duty—by this one can reach the royal pinnacle.

sentences.zh: 故其彝訓曰：'後克艱厥後，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂。

translations.literal: Therefore their constant instruction says: 'If the ruler can make his rule arduous, if ministers can make their service arduous, governance is ordered.'
translations.idiomatic: Therefore their constant instruction says: 'If the ruler can make his rule arduous, if ministers can make their service arduous, governance is ordered.'

sentences.zh: '今台一人，膺天之嘏，既陟元後。

translations.literal: Now I alone have received Heaven's blessing and ascended as chief ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Now I alone have received Heaven's blessing and ascended as chief ruler.

sentences.zh: 股肱百辟，乂服我國家之命，罔不咸守厥職。

translations.literal: Arms, legs, and hundred ministers all obey the charge of our state—none fails to keep his post.
translations.idiomatic: Arms, legs, and hundred ministers all obey the charge of our state—none fails to keep his post.

sentences.zh: 嗟！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 後弗艱厥後，臣弗艱厥臣，政于何弗斁？

translations.literal: If the ruler does not make his rule arduous, if ministers do not make their service arduous—how shall governance not decay?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler does not make his rule arduous, if ministers do not make their service arduous—how shall governance not decay?

sentences.zh: 嗚呼艱哉！

translations.literal: Ah, how arduous!
translations.idiomatic: Ah, how arduous!

sentences.zh: 凡爾在位，其敬聽命。」

translations.literal: All you who hold office—reverently hear the charge."
translations.idiomatic: All you who hold office—reverently hear the charge."

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「柱國，惟四海之不造，載繇二紀。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not prospered for nearly two reign-periods.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Pillar of State, the realm has not prospered for nearly two reign-periods.

sentences.zh: 天未絕我太祖、烈祖之命，用錫我以元輔。

translations.literal: Heaven has not cut short the mandate of our Grand Ancestor and Resolute Ancestor and has granted me you as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has not cut short the mandate of our Grand Ancestor and Resolute Ancestor and has granted me you as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 國家將附，公惟棟樑。

translations.literal: When the state was about to collapse, you were its pillar and beam.
translations.idiomatic: When the state was about to collapse, you were its pillar and beam.

sentences.zh: 皇之弗極，公惟作相。

translations.literal: When the throne lacked its pinnacle, you served as chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: When the throne lacked its pinnacle, you served as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 百揆愆度，公惟大錄。

translations.literal: When the hundred affairs lost measure, you greatly restored order.
translations.idiomatic: When the hundred affairs lost measure, you greatly restored order.

sentences.zh: 公其允文允武，克明克乂，迪七德，敷九功，龕暴除亂，下綏我蒼生，傍施於九正，若伊之在商，周之有呂，說之相丁，用保我無疆之祚。」

translations.literal: Be truly civil and truly martial, able to illumine and able to order; practice the seven virtues and spread the nine achievements; pacify violence and remove chaos, settle our common people below, and extend to the nine directions—like Yi in Yin, Lü in Zhou, and Yue assisting Ding—to preserve our boundless fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Be truly civil and truly martial, able to illumine and able to order; practice the seven virtues and spread the nine achievements; pacify violence and remove chaos, settle our common people below, and extend to the nine directions—like Yi in Yin, Lü in Zhou, and Yue assisting Ding—to preserve our boundless fortune."

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「群公、太宰、太尉、司徒、司空。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Dukes, Grand Steward, Grand Commandant, Minister of the Masses, Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Dukes, Grand Steward, Grand Commandant, Minister of the Masses, Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 惟公作朕鼎足，以弼乎朕躬。

translations.literal: You serve as my tripod legs to assist my person.
translations.idiomatic: You serve as my tripod legs to assist my person.

sentences.zh: 宰惟天官，克諧六職。

translations.literal: The Steward is Heaven's officer and harmonizes the six duties.
translations.idiomatic: The Steward is Heaven's officer and harmonizes the six duties.

sentences.zh: 尉惟司武，武在止戈。

translations.literal: The Commandant governs the martial; the martial lies in stopping weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The Commandant governs the martial; the martial lies in stopping weapons.

sentences.zh: 徒惟司眾，敬敷五教。

translations.literal: The Minister of the Masses governs the multitude and reverently spreads the five teachings.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Masses governs the multitude and reverently spreads the five teachings.

sentences.zh: 空惟司土，利用厚生。

translations.literal: The Minister of Works governs the land and employs it to enrich life.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Works governs the land and employs it to enrich life.

sentences.zh: 惟時三事，若三階之在天；

translations.literal: These three affairs are like the three steps in heaven;
translations.idiomatic: These three affairs are like the three steps in heaven;

sentences.zh: 惟茲四輔，若四時之成歲。

translations.literal: these four assistants are like the four seasons completing the year.
translations.idiomatic: these four assistants are like the four seasons completing the year.

sentences.zh: 天工人其代諸。」

translations.literal: Heaven's work—will you not take it in hand?"
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's work—will you not take it in hand?"

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「列將，汝惟鷹揚，作朕爪牙。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Generals, you are the soaring hawk and serve as my claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Generals, you are the soaring hawk and serve as my claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 寇賊奸宄，蠻夷猾夏，汝徂征。

translations.literal: Bandits, rebels, and traitors; barbarians troubling the heartland—you go forth to campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits, rebels, and traitors; barbarians troubling the heartland—you go forth to campaign.

sentences.zh: 綏之以惠，董之以威，刑期無刑，萬邦咸寧。

translations.literal: Soothe with kindness, oversee with awe; punishments aim at no punishments; the myriad states all find peace.
translations.idiomatic: Soothe with kindness, oversee with awe; punishments aim at no punishments; the myriad states all find peace.

sentences.zh: 俾八表之內，莫違朕命，時汝功。」

translations.literal: Make it so that within the eight directions none disobeys my command—this is your achievement."
translations.idiomatic: Make it so that within the eight directions none disobeys my command—this is your achievement."

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「庶邦列辟，汝惟守土，作人父母。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Feudal lords of the myriad states, you guard the land and are parents to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Feudal lords of the myriad states, you guard the land and are parents to the people.

sentences.zh: 人惟不勝其饑，故先王重農；

translations.literal: People cannot overcome hunger—therefore former kings valued farming;
translations.idiomatic: People cannot overcome hunger—therefore former kings valued farming;

sentences.zh: 不勝其寒，故先王貴女工。

translations.literal: they cannot overcome cold—therefore former kings honored women's work.
translations.idiomatic: they cannot overcome cold—therefore former kings honored women's work.

sentences.zh: 人之不率於孝慈，則骨肉之恩薄；

translations.literal: When people do not lead in filial piety and kindness, ties of flesh and bone grow thin;
translations.idiomatic: When people do not lead in filial piety and kindness, ties of flesh and bone grow thin;

sentences.zh: 弗惇於禮讓，則爭奪之萌生。

translations.literal: when they are not earnest in ritual and deference, contention and seizure arise.
translations.idiomatic: when they are not earnest in ritual and deference, contention and seizure arise.

sentences.zh: 惟茲六物，實為教本。

translations.literal: These six things are truly the root of instruction.
translations.idiomatic: These six things are truly the root of instruction.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 為上在寬，寬則人怠，齊之以禮，不剛不柔，稽極於道。」

translations.literal: In governing, leniency is primary; if too lenient people grow slack—align them with ritual, neither hard nor soft, and measure to the utmost of the Way."
translations.idiomatic: In governing, leniency is primary; if too lenient people grow slack—align them with ritual, neither hard nor soft, and measure to the utmost of the Way."

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「卿士、庶尹、凡百禦事，王省惟歲，卿士惟月，庶尹惟日，禦事惟時。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Officers, various directors, and all attendants—the king examines by the year, officers by the month, directors by the day, attendants by the hour.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Officers, various directors, and all attendants—the king examines by the year, officers by the month, directors by the day, attendants by the hour.

sentences.zh: 歲月日時，罔易其度，百憲咸貞，庶績其凝。

translations.literal: Year, month, day, and hour—do not alter their measure; the hundred statutes all hold true and myriad achievements coalesce.
translations.idiomatic: Year, month, day, and hour—do not alter their measure; the hundred statutes all hold true and myriad achievements coalesce.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Ah!
translations.idiomatic: Ah!

sentences.zh: 惟若王官，陶均萬國，若天之有鬥，斟元氣，酌陰陽，弗失其和，蒼生永賴；

translations.literal: You royal officers blend and balance the myriad states like heaven's Dipper, measuring primal qi and adjusting yin and yang—do not lose harmony and the common people will forever rely on you;
translations.idiomatic: You royal officers blend and balance the myriad states like heaven's Dipper, measuring primal qi and adjusting yin and yang—do not lose harmony and the common people will forever rely on you;

sentences.zh: 悖其序，萬物以傷。

translations.literal: violate their order and the myriad things are harmed.
translations.idiomatic: violate their order and the myriad things are harmed.

translations.literal: The times are arduous indeed!"
translations.idiomatic: The times are arduous indeed!"

sentences.zh: 皇帝若曰：「惟天地之道，一陰一陽；

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The Way of heaven and earth is one yin and one yang;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The Way of heaven and earth is one yin and one yang;

sentences.zh: 禮俗之變，一文一質。

translations.literal: changes in ritual and custom are one ornament and one plainness.
translations.idiomatic: changes in ritual and custom are one ornament and one plainness.

sentences.zh: 爰自三五，以迄於茲，匪惟相革，惟其救弊；

translations.literal: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors down to now, it is not only mutual change but saving what is decayed;
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors down to now, it is not only mutual change but saving what is decayed;

sentences.zh: 匪惟相襲，惟其可久。

translations.literal: not only mutual succession but what can endure.
translations.idiomatic: not only mutual succession but what can endure.

sentences.zh: 惟我有魏，承乎周之末流，接秦、漢遺弊，襲魏、晉之華誕，五代澆風，因而未革，將以穆俗興化，庸可暨乎！

translations.literal: Our Wei inherited the late stream of Zhou, received the leftover abuses of Qin and Han, and took over the ornate extravagance of Wei and Jin—five reigns of shallow custom still unreformed; to solemnify custom and raise transformation—how can one reach that!
translations.idiomatic: Our Wei inherited the late stream of Zhou, received the leftover abuses of Qin and Han, and took over the ornate extravagance of Wei and Jin—five reigns of shallow custom still unreformed; to solemnify custom and raise transformation—how can one reach that!

sentences.zh: 嗟我公輔、庶僚、列辟，朕惟否德，其一朕心力，祗慎厥艱，克遵前王之丕顯休烈，弗敢怠荒。

translations.literal: Alas, my chief ministers, various officials, and feudal lords—I am of little virtue but will exhaust my heart and strength, reverently heed the arduous, and be able to follow the great bright glorious merit of former kings without daring slackness or dissipation.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, my chief ministers, various officials, and feudal lords—I am of little virtue but will exhaust my heart and strength, reverently heed the arduous, and be able to follow the great bright glorious merit of former kings without daring slackness or dissipation.

sentences.zh: 咨爾在位，亦協於朕心，惇德允元，惟厥艱是務。

translations.literal: Consult you who hold office—also align with my heart; be sincere in virtue and truly foundational; make the arduous your task.
translations.idiomatic: Consult you who hold office—also align with my heart; be sincere in virtue and truly foundational; make the arduous your task.

sentences.zh: 克捐厥華，即厥實，背厥偽，崇厥誠。

translations.literal: Able to discard ornament, take up substance, turn from falsity, and honor sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: Able to discard ornament, take up substance, turn from falsity, and honor sincerity.

sentences.zh: 勿愆勿忘，一乎三代之彝典，歸於道德仁義，用保我祖宗之丕命。

translations.literal: Do not err, do not forget—be one with the constant canon of the Three Dynasties, return to virtue, morality, benevolence, and righteousness, and thereby preserve the great mandate of our ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: Do not err, do not forget—be one with the constant canon of the Three Dynasties, return to virtue, morality, benevolence, and righteousness, and thereby preserve the great mandate of our ancestors.

sentences.zh: 荷天之休，克綏我萬方，永康我黎庶。

translations.literal: Receive Heaven's blessing, able to settle our myriad regions, and forever secure our common people.
translations.idiomatic: Receive Heaven's blessing, able to settle our myriad regions, and forever secure our common people.

sentences.zh: 戒之哉，朕言不再。」

translations.literal: Take warning—my words will not be spoken again."
translations.idiomatic: Take warning—my words will not be spoken again."

sentences.zh: 柱國泰洎庶僚百辟拜手稽首曰：「'亶聰明，作元後，元後作人父母'。

translations.literal: The Pillar of State Tai and the various officials and hundred ministers bowed with hands joined and heads to the ground, saying: "'Truly wise and clear, serving as chief ruler—the chief ruler is parent to the people.
translations.idiomatic: The Pillar of State Tai and the various officials and hundred ministers bowed with hands joined and heads to the ground, saying: "'Truly wise and clear, serving as chief ruler—the chief ruler is parent to the people.

sentences.zh: 惟三五之王，率繇此道，用臻于刑措。

translations.literal: Only the kings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors all followed this Way and reached the point where punishments were set aside.
translations.idiomatic: Only the kings of the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors all followed this Way and reached the point where punishments were set aside.

sentences.zh: 自時厥後，曆千載未聞。

translations.literal: From that time until now, a thousand years have passed without hearing of it.
translations.idiomatic: From that time until now, a thousand years have passed without hearing of it.

sentences.zh: 惟帝念功，將反叔世，逖致於雍熙，庸錫降丕命於我群臣。

translations.literal: Only the emperor mindful of merit will turn back the declining age and from afar bring great harmony—thereby graciously bestowing a great charge upon us ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Only the emperor mindful of merit will turn back the declining age and from afar bring great harmony—thereby graciously bestowing a great charge upon us ministers.

sentences.zh: 博哉王言，非言之難，行之實難。

translations.literal: How broad are the king's words—not speaking is hard, but doing is truly hard.
translations.idiomatic: How broad are the king's words—not speaking is hard, but doing is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 臣聞'靡不有初，鮮克有終'。

translations.literal: We ministers have heard: 'Nothing lacks a beginning, but few reach the end.'
translations.idiomatic: We ministers have heard: 'Nothing lacks a beginning, but few reach the end.'

sentences.zh: 商書曰；

translations.literal: The Book of Shang says:
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Shang says:

sentences.zh: '終始惟一，德乃日新。

translations.literal: From end to beginning be one—then virtue daily renews.
translations.idiomatic: From end to beginning be one—then virtue daily renews.

sentences.zh: '惟帝敬厥始，慎厥終，以躋日新之德，則我群臣，敢不夙夜對揚休哉！

translations.literal: If the emperor reverently attends the beginning and carefully guards the end, ascending to daily-renewing virtue—how dare we ministers not from early dawn to night respond and proclaim this blessing!
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor reverently attends the beginning and carefully guards the end, ascending to daily-renewing virtue—how dare we ministers not from early dawn to night respond and proclaim this blessing!

sentences.zh: 惟茲大誼，未光於四表，以邁種德，俾九域幽遐，咸昭奉元後之明訓，率遷於道，永膺無疆之休。」

translations.literal: May this great principle shine to the four quarters, advance the planting of virtue, and make the nine regions however remote all clearly receive the chief ruler's bright instruction, follow the Way in turn, and forever receive boundless blessing.'"
translations.idiomatic: May this great principle shine to the four quarters, advance the planting of virtue, and make the nine regions however remote all clearly receive the chief ruler's bright instruction, follow the Way in turn, and forever receive boundless blessing.'"

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「欽哉。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Reverently heed it."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Reverently heed it."

sentences.zh: 自是之後，文筆皆依此體。

translations.literal: From then on, all writing followed this style.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, all writing followed this style.

sentences.zh: 綽性儉素，不事產業，家無餘財。

translations.literal: Chuo was frugal and plain by nature, did not pursue property, and his household had no surplus wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo was frugal and plain by nature, did not pursue property, and his household had no surplus wealth.

sentences.zh: 以海內未平，常以天下為已任。

translations.literal: Because the realm within the seas was not yet pacified, he always took the world as his own responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Because the realm was not yet pacified, he always took the world as his own responsibility.

sentences.zh: 博求賢俊，共弘政道，凡所薦達，皆至大官。

translations.literal: He broadly sought the worthy and talented to jointly promote the way of governance; all he recommended reached high office.
translations.idiomatic: He broadly sought the worthy and talented to jointly promote the way of governance; all he recommended reached high office.

sentences.zh: 周文亦推心委任，而無間言焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou also entrusted him wholeheartedly, and there was no whisper of distrust.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou also entrusted him wholeheartedly, and there was no whisper of distrust.

sentences.zh: 或出遊，常預署空紙以授綽，若須有處分，則隨事施行。

translations.literal: When going out on tour he often pre-signed blank paper and gave it to Chuo; if disposition was needed, Chuo acted according to the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When going out on tour he often pre-signed blank paper and gave it to Chuo; if disposition was needed, Chuo acted according to the matter.

sentences.zh: 及還，啟知而已。

translations.literal: When he returned, Chuo merely reported what had been done.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, Chuo merely reported what had been done.

sentences.zh: 綽常謂為國之道，當愛人如慈父，訓人如嚴師。

translations.literal: Chuo often said that the way to govern a state is to love people like a kindly father and instruct them like a strict teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo often said that the way to govern a state is to love people like a kindly father and instruct them like a strict teacher.

sentences.zh: 每與公卿議論，自晝達夜，事無巨細，若指諸掌。

translations.literal: Whenever he discussed affairs with dukes and ministers, from day into night, nothing great or small escaped him—as if pointing at his palm.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he discussed affairs with dukes and ministers, from day into night, nothing great or small escaped him—as if it were all in the palm of his hand.

sentences.zh: 積思勞倦，遂成氣疾。

translations.literal: Accumulated thought and weariness finally produced a disorder of qi.
translations.idiomatic: Accumulated thought and weariness finally produced a disorder of qi.

sentences.zh: 十二年，卒于位，時年四十九。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he died in office at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he died in office at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 周文痛惜之，哀動左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou grieved deeply; his sorrow moved those around him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou grieved deeply; his sorrow moved those around him.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，乃謂公卿等曰：「蘇尚書平生謙退，敦尚儉約。

translations.literal: When the burial was about to take place, he said to the dukes and ministers: "Director Su was modest all his life and devoted to thrift.
translations.idiomatic: When the burial was about to take place, he said to the dukes and ministers: "Director Su was modest all his life and devoted to thrift.

sentences.zh: 吾欲全其素志，便恐悠悠之徒，有所未達；

translations.literal: I wish to preserve his lifelong intent, yet I fear idle gossips may not understand;
translations.idiomatic: I wish to preserve his lifelong intent, yet I fear idle gossips may not understand;

sentences.zh: 如其厚加贈諡，又乖宿昔相知之道。

translations.literal: if I richly add posthumous honors, that also goes against our old mutual understanding.
translations.idiomatic: if I richly add posthumous honors, that also goes against our old mutual understanding.

sentences.zh: 進退惟穀，孤有疑焉。」

translations.literal: Advance or retreat—I alone am in doubt."
translations.idiomatic: Advance or retreat—I alone am in doubt."

sentences.zh: 尚書令史麻瑤越次而進曰：「或晏子，齊之賢大夫，一狐裘三十年。

translations.literal: Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Ma Yao stepped forward out of turn and said: "Yanzi of Qi, that worthy grandee, wore one fox fur coat for thirty years.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk of the Secretariat Ma Yao stepped forward out of turn and said: "Yanzi of Qi, that worthy grandee, wore one fox fur coat for thirty years.

sentences.zh: 及其死也，遣車一乘。

translations.literal: When he died, only one carriage followed his coffin.
translations.idiomatic: When he died, only one carriage followed his coffin.

sentences.zh: 齊侯不奪其志。

translations.literal: The Lord of Qi did not override his intent.
translations.idiomatic: The Lord of Qi did not override his intent.

sentences.zh: 綽既操履清白，廉挹自居，愚謂宜從儉約，以彰其美。」

translations.literal: Since Chuo's conduct was pure and white and he lived in modest restraint, I think thrift should be followed to display his virtue."
translations.idiomatic: Since Chuo's conduct was pure and he lived in modest restraint, I think thrift should be followed to display his virtue."

sentences.zh: 周文稱善，因薦瑤於朝廷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised this and thereupon recommended Yao to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou praised this and thereupon recommended Yao to the court.

sentences.zh: 及綽歸葬武功，唯載，以布車一乘。

translations.literal: When Chuo was buried in Wugong, only his coffin was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuo was buried in Wugong, only his coffin was carried on a single cloth-covered cart.

sentences.zh: 周文與群公，皆步送出同州郭外。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou and the assembled dukes all walked to escort him beyond the walls of Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou and the assembled dukes all walked to escort him beyond the walls of Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 周文親于車後酹酒而言曰：「尚書平生為事，妻子兄弟不知者，吾皆知之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen personally poured libation behind the cart and said: "In what Director did all his life, what his wife, children, and brothers did not know—I know it all.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen personally poured libation behind the cart and said: "In what Director did all his life, what his wife, children, and brothers did not know—I know it all.

sentences.zh: 惟爾知吾心，吾知爾意。

translations.literal: Only you know my heart; I know your intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only you know my heart; I know your intent.

sentences.zh: 方欲共定天下，不幸遂舍吾去，奈何！」

translations.literal: We were just about to settle the realm together—unfortunately you have left me. What can be done!"
translations.idiomatic: We were just about to settle the realm together—unfortunately you have left me. What can be done!"

sentences.zh: 因舉聲慟哭，不覺卮墜於手。

translations.literal: He then raised his voice in bitter weeping, and before he knew it the cup fell from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He then raised his voice in bitter weeping, and before he knew it the cup fell from his hand.

sentences.zh: 至葬日，又遣使祭乙太牢，周文自為其文。

translations.literal: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice with a full ox; Emperor Wen of Zhou wrote the text himself.
translations.idiomatic: On the burial day he again sent an envoy to sacrifice with a full ox; Emperor Wen of Zhou wrote the text himself.

sentences.zh: 綽又著佛性論、七經論，並行於世。

translations.literal: Chuo also wrote Treatise on Buddha-nature and Treatise on the Seven Classics, both circulated in his time.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo also wrote Treatise on Buddha-nature and Treatise on the Seven Classics, both circulated in his time.

sentences.zh: 周明帝二年，以綽配享文帝廟廷。

translations.literal: In the second year of Emperor Ming of Zhou, Chuo was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Emperor Ming of Zhou, Chuo was given paired sacrifice in Emperor Wen's temple hall.

sentences.zh: 子威嗣。

translations.literal: His son Wei inherited his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Wei inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 威字無畏。

translations.literal: Wei, courtesy name Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, courtesy name Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 少有至性，五歲喪父，哀毀有若成人。

translations.literal: From youth he had utmost sincerity; at five he lost his father and mourned with grief like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had utmost sincerity; at five he lost his father and mourned with grief like an adult.

sentences.zh: 周文帝時，襲爵美陽縣公，仕郡功曹。

translations.literal: During Emperor Wen of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Meiyang County and served as Merit Officer of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During Emperor Wen of Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Meiyang County and served as Merit Officer of the commandery.

sentences.zh: 大塚宰宇文護見而禮之，以其女新興公主妻焉。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu saw him and honored him, giving him his daughter Princess Xinxing in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Preceptor Yuwen Hu saw him and honored him, giving him his daughter Princess Xinxing in marriage.

sentences.zh: 威見護專權，恐禍及已，逃入山。

translations.literal: Wei saw that Hu monopolized power and, fearing disaster would reach him, fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wei saw that Hu monopolized power and, fearing disaster would reach him, fled into the mountains.

sentences.zh: 為叔父所逼，卒不獲免。

translations.literal: Pressed by his uncle, he ultimately could not escape.
translations.idiomatic: Pressed by his uncle, he ultimately could not escape.

sentences.zh: 然每居山寺，以諷讀為娛。

translations.literal: Yet whenever he stayed in mountain temples, he took chanting and reading as his recreation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever he stayed in mountain temples, he took chanting and reading as his recreation.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授持節、車騎大將軍、儀同三司，改封懷道縣公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huaidao County.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Bearer of the Staff, General of Chariots and Cavalry, and Equal in Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and enfeoffed as Duke of Huaidao County.

sentences.zh: 武帝親總萬機，拜稍伯下大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Wei was appointed Grand Master of Shaobo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, Wei was appointed Grand Master of Shaobo.

sentences.zh: 前後所授，並辭疾不拜。

translations.literal: All appointments before and after he declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: All appointments before and after he declined on grounds of illness and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 有從父妹適河南元世雄。

translations.literal: He had a younger female cousin by marriage who wedded Yuan Shixiong of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: He had a younger female cousin by marriage who wedded Yuan Shixiong of Henan.

sentences.zh: 世雄先與突厥有隙，突厥入朝，請世雄及其妻子，將甘心焉。

translations.literal: Shixiong had earlier had a feud with the Turks; when the Turks came to court they requested Shixiong and his wife and children, intending to have their fill of revenge.
translations.idiomatic: Shixiong had earlier had a feud with the Turks; when the Turks came to court they requested Shixiong and his wife and children, intending to have their fill of revenge.

sentences.zh: 周遂遣之。

translations.literal: Zhou thereupon sent them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou thereupon sent them.

sentences.zh: 威以夷人昧利，遂標賣田宅，罄資產贖世雄。

translations.literal: Wei, reasoning that barbarians covet profit, posted notices selling his fields and houses and exhausted his assets to ransom Shixiong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei, reasoning that barbarians covet profit, posted notices selling his fields and houses and exhausted his assets to ransom Shixiong.

sentences.zh: 論者義之。

translations.literal: Commentators praised his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators praised his righteousness.

sentences.zh: 宣帝嗣位，就拜開府。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Wei was immediately appointed Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Wei was immediately appointed Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，高熲屢言其賢，亦素重其名，召入臥內，與語大悅。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Gao Jiong repeatedly spoke of his worth; he also long valued Wei's name, summoned him to his private chamber, and was greatly pleased in conversation.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Sui was chief minister, Gao Jiong repeatedly spoke of his worth; he also long valued Wei's name, summoned him to his private chamber, and was greatly pleased in conversation.

sentences.zh: 居月餘，威聞禪代之議，遁歸田里。

translations.literal: After more than a month Wei heard talk of abdication and the transfer of the mandate and fled back to his fields.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Wei heard talk of abdication and the transfer of the mandate and fled back to his fields.

sentences.zh: 高熲請追之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong asked to pursue him.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong asked to pursue him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「此不欲預吾事，且置之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "He does not wish to take part in my affairs—for now leave him be."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "He does not wish to take part in my affairs—for now leave him be."

sentences.zh: 及受禪，徵拜太子少保，追贈其父邳國公，以威襲焉。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Wei was summoned as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; his father was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pi, and Wei inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: When he received the abdication, Wei was summoned as Junior Tutor to the Crown Prince; his father was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Pi, and Wei inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 俄兼納言，威上表陳讓，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he additionally served as Palace Director; Wei memorialized declining, but a gracious edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he additionally served as Palace Director; Wei memorialized declining, but a gracious edict would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗與文獻皇后對觴，召威及高熲、楊素、廣平王雄四人，謂曰：「太史言朕祚運盡於三年，朕憂懣，故舉此酒耳。

translations.literal: The emperor once drank facing Empress Wenxian and summoned Wei, Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and Prince Xiong of Guangping, saying: "The Grand Astrologer says my fortune ends in three years—I am troubled and depressed, and therefore raise this cup.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once drank facing Empress Wenxian and summoned Wei, Gao Jiong, Yang Su, and Prince Xiong of Guangping, saying: "The Grand Astrologer says my fortune ends in three years—I am troubled and depressed, and therefore raise this cup.

sentences.zh: 今欲營南山險處，與公等固之，以觀時變，將如何？」

translations.literal: Now I wish to fortify a defensible place in the southern mountains with you and hold it to watch how times change—what do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to fortify a defensible place in the southern mountains with you and hold it to watch how times change—what do you think?"

sentences.zh: 威進曰：「周文修德，旋地動之災；

translations.literal: Wei stepped forward and said: "When Emperor Wen of Zhou cultivated virtue, the disaster of earthquakes soon ceased;
translations.idiomatic: Wei stepped forward and said: "When Emperor Wen of Zhou cultivated virtue, the disaster of earthquakes soon ceased;

sentences.zh: 宋景一言，退法星三舍。

translations.literal: one word from Song Jing made the Punishment Star retreat three lodges.
translations.idiomatic: one word from Song Jing made the Punishment Star retreat three lodges.

sentences.zh: 願陛下恢崇德度，享天之休。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would broadly exalt virtue and enjoy Heaven's blessing.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would broadly exalt virtue and enjoy Heaven's blessing.

sentences.zh: 若棄德恃險，同舟之人，誰非敵國！

translations.literal: If you abandon virtue and rely on defiles, among those in the same boat—who is not a potential enemy!
translations.idiomatic: If you abandon virtue and rely on defiles, among those in the same boat—who is not a potential enemy!

sentences.zh: 縱南山之岨，安足固哉？」

translations.literal: Even the steep heights of the southern mountains—how could they truly be secure?"
translations.idiomatic: Even the steep heights of the southern mountains—how could they truly be secure?"

sentences.zh: 帝善其言，屬之以酒。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his words and handed him wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his words and handed him wine.

sentences.zh: 初，威父綽在魏，以國用不足，為徵稅法，頗稱為重。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Wei's father Chuo was in Wei, because state revenue was insufficient he devised a tax-collection law that was widely called heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wei's father Chuo was in Wei, because state revenue was insufficient he devised a tax-collection law that was widely called heavy.

sentences.zh: 既而歎曰：「所為者正如張弓，非平世法也。

translations.literal: Later he sighed and said: "What I have done is like drawing a bow too tight—it is not the law of a peaceful age.
translations.idiomatic: Later he sighed and said: "What I have done is like drawing a bow too tight—it is not the law of a peaceful age.

sentences.zh: 後之君子，誰能馳乎？」

translations.literal: Which gentleman of later times will be able to release it?"
translations.idiomatic: Which gentleman of later times will be able to release it?"

sentences.zh: 威聞其言，每以為己任。

translations.literal: When Wei heard these words he always took them as his own task.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei heard these words he always took them as his own task.

sentences.zh: 至是，奏減賦役，務從輕典，帝悉從之。

translations.literal: At this time he memorialized to reduce levies and corvée, striving for lighter statutes, and the emperor followed all of it.
translations.idiomatic: At this time he memorialized to reduce levies and corvée, striving for lighter statutes, and the emperor followed all of it.

sentences.zh: 漸見親重，與高熲參掌朝政。

translations.literal: He gradually came to be personally valued and with Gao Jiong jointly managed court governance.
translations.idiomatic: He gradually came to be personally valued and with Gao Jiong jointly managed court governance.

sentences.zh: 威見宮中以銀為幔鉤，因盛陳節儉之美，諭帝。

translations.literal: Wei saw silver used for curtain hooks in the palace and thereupon greatly expounded the beauty of thrift to instruct the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei saw silver used for curtain hooks in the palace and thereupon greatly expounded the beauty of thrift to instruct the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝為改容，雕飾舊物，悉命除毀。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression; carved and decorated old objects were all ordered removed and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor changed expression; carved and decorated old objects were all ordered removed and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗怒一人，將殺之。

translations.literal: The emperor once grew angry at a man and was about to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once grew angry at a man and was about to kill him.

sentences.zh: 威入閣進諫，不納。

translations.literal: Wei entered the inner chamber to remonstrate but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Wei entered the inner chamber to remonstrate but was not heeded.

sentences.zh: 帝怒甚，將自出斬之。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and was about to go out himself to behead the man.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and was about to go out himself to behead the man.

sentences.zh: 威當前不去，帝避之而出。

translations.literal: Wei stood in front and would not leave; the emperor sidestepped him and went out.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stood in front and would not leave; the emperor sidestepped him and went out.

sentences.zh: 威又遮止帝，帝拂衣入。

translations.literal: Wei again blocked and stopped the emperor; the emperor brushed his robes and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Wei again blocked and stopped the emperor; the emperor brushed his robes and entered.

sentences.zh: 良久，乃召威謝曰：「公能若是，吾無憂矣。」

translations.literal: After a long while he summoned Wei and apologized, saying: "If you can be like this, I have no worries."
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he summoned Wei and apologized, saying: "If you can be like this, I have no worries."

sentences.zh: 於是賜馬二匹、錢十餘萬。

translations.literal: He then bestowed two horses and more than a hundred thousand in cash.
translations.idiomatic: He then bestowed two horses and more than a hundred thousand in cash.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，尋復兼大理卿、京兆尹、御史大夫，本官悉如故。

translations.literal: After more than a year he soon again concurrently served as Director of the Court of Justice, Governor of Jingzhao, and Censor-in-Chief; his original posts all remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he soon again concurrently served as Director of the Court of Justice, Governor of Jingzhao, and Censor-in-Chief; his original posts all remained as before.

sentences.zh: 持書侍御史梁毗劾威兼領五職，安繁戀劇，無舉賢自代心。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Censor Liang Pi impeached Wei for holding five posts concurrently, clinging to complexity and busyness, and lacking the will to recommend the worthy to succeed him.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Attendant Censor Liang Pi impeached Wei for holding five posts concurrently, clinging to complexity and busyness, and lacking the will to recommend the worthy to succeed him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「蘇威朝夕孜孜，志存遠大，舉賢有闕，何遽迫之。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Su Wei is diligent from morning to night with far-reaching intent; if recommending the worthy has gaps, why press him so soon?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Su Wei is diligent from morning to night with far-reaching intent; if recommending the worthy has gaps, why press him so soon?"

sentences.zh: 顧謂威曰：「用之則行，舍之則藏，唯我與爾有是夫！」

translations.literal: Turning to Wei he said: "Employed, then act; set aside, then withdraw—only you and I have this!"
translations.idiomatic: Turning to Wei he said: "Employed, then act; set aside, then withdraw—only you and I have this!"

sentences.zh: 因謂朝臣曰：「蘇威不遇我，無以措其言；

translations.literal: He then said to the court ministers: "Without meeting me, Su Wei would have nowhere to place his words;
translations.idiomatic: He then said to the court ministers: "Without meeting me, Su Wei would have nowhere to place his words;

sentences.zh: 我不得蘇威，何以行其道？

translations.literal: without Su Wei, how could I practice my Way?
translations.idiomatic: without Su Wei, how could I practice my Way?

sentences.zh: 楊素才辯無雙，至若斟酌古今，助我宣化，非威匹也。

translations.literal: Yang Su's talent and eloquence are unmatched, but when it comes to weighing past and present and helping me spread transformation, he is not Wei's equal.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su's talent and eloquence are unmatched, but when it comes to weighing past and present and helping me spread transformation, he is not Wei's equal.

sentences.zh: 蘇威若逢亂世，商山四皓，豈易屈哉！」

translations.literal: If Su Wei met chaotic times, like the Four Whiteheads of Mount Shang—would he be easily bent!"
translations.idiomatic: If Su Wei met chaotic times, like the Four Whiteheads of Mount Shang—would he be easily bent!"

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: Such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜刑部尚書，解少保、御史大夫官。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice and relieved of the posts of Junior Tutor and Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Director of the Ministry of Justice and relieved of the posts of Junior Tutor and Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 後京兆尹廢，檢校雍州別駕。

translations.literal: Later when the governorship of Jingzhao was abolished, he served as Acting Vice Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later when the governorship of Jingzhao was abolished, he served as Acting Vice Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時高熲與威同心，協贊政刑，大小無不籌之，故革運數年，天下稱平。

translations.literal: At the time Gao Jiong and Wei were of one mind, jointly supporting governance and law; nothing great or small was not planned by them, and therefore within a few years of the change of dynasty the realm was called peaceful.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Gao Jiong and Wei were of one mind, jointly supporting governance and law; nothing great or small was not planned by them, and therefore within a few years of the change of dynasty the realm was called peaceful.

sentences.zh: 俄轉戶部尚書，納言如故。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Revenue while remaining Palace Director as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Revenue while remaining Palace Director as before.

sentences.zh: 屬山東諸州人饑，帝令威振恤之。

translations.literal: When people in the eastern provinces suffered famine, the emperor ordered Wei to relieve and succor them.
translations.idiomatic: When people in the eastern provinces suffered famine, the emperor ordered Wei to relieve and succor them.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部尚書，兼領國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently head of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel and concurrently head of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 隋承戰爭之後，憲章踳駁。

translations.literal: Sui inherited the aftermath of war; statutes and regulations were confused and contradictory.
translations.idiomatic: Sui inherited the aftermath of war; statutes and regulations were confused and contradictory.

sentences.zh: 帝令朝臣厘改舊法，為一代通典，律令格式多威所定。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered court ministers to revise old laws into a general canon for the age; much of the code of statutes, commands, forms, and rules was set by Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered court ministers to revise old laws into a general canon for the age; much of the code of statutes, commands, forms, and rules was set by Wei.

sentences.zh: 世以為能。

translations.literal: The age considered him capable.
translations.idiomatic: The age considered him capable.

sentences.zh: 九年，拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 其年，以母憂去職，柴毀骨立。

translations.literal: That year, on his mother's death he left office; his mourning grief wasted him to skin and bone.
translations.idiomatic: That year, on his mother's death he left office; his mourning grief wasted him to skin and bone.

sentences.zh: 敕勉諭殷勤，未幾，起令視事。

translations.literal: An edict urged and consoled him earnestly; before long he was recalled to resume duties.
translations.idiomatic: An edict urged and consoled him earnestly; before long he was recalled to resume duties.

sentences.zh: 固辭，優詔不許。

translations.literal: He firmly declined, but a gracious edict would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly declined, but a gracious edict would not permit it.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝幸并州，命與高熲同總留事。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor visited Bingzhou and ordered Wei together with Gao Jiong to oversee all remaining affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year the emperor visited Bingzhou and ordered Wei together with Gao Jiong to oversee all remaining affairs.

sentences.zh: 俄追詣行在所，使決人訟。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned to the emperor's camp and made to decide people's lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was summoned to the emperor's camp and made to decide people's lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 尋令持節巡撫江南，得以便宜從事。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was ordered to tour and pacify Jiangnan bearing the staff and was permitted to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was ordered to tour and pacify Jiangnan bearing the staff and was permitted to act as expedient required.

sentences.zh: 過會稽，逾五嶺而還。

translations.literal: He passed Kuaiji, crossed the Five Ridges, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He passed Kuaiji, crossed the Five Ridges, and returned.

sentences.zh: 江表自晉已來，刑法疏緩，代族貴賤，不相陵越。

translations.literal: South of the Yangzi since Jin, penal law had been loose and mild; noble and common clans did not overstep one another.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi since Jin, penal law had been loose and mild; noble and common clans did not overstep one another.

sentences.zh: 平陳之後，牧人者盡改變之，無長幼悉使誦五教。

translations.literal: After Chen was pacified, those who governed the people changed all this; young and old alike were made to recite the Five Teachings.
translations.idiomatic: After Chen was pacified, those who governed the people changed all this; young and old alike were made to recite the Five Teachings.

sentences.zh: 威加以煩鄙之辭，百姓嗟怨。

translations.literal: Wei added tedious and vulgar words, and the people sighed with resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Wei added tedious and vulgar words, and the people sighed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 使還，奏言江表依內州責戶籍。

translations.literal: When he returned from his mission he memorialized that the south of the Yangzi should be charged for household registers like the inner provinces.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from his mission he memorialized that the south of the Yangzi should be charged for household registers like the inner provinces.

sentences.zh: 上以江表初平，召戶部尚書張嬰，責以政急。

translations.literal: Because the south of the Yangzi had only just been pacified, the emperor summoned Director of Revenue Zhang Ying and rebuked him for harsh governance.
translations.idiomatic: Because the south of the Yangzi had only just been pacified, the emperor summoned Director of Revenue Zhang Ying and rebuked him for harsh governance.

sentences.zh: 時江南州縣又論言欲徙之入關，遠近驚駭。

translations.literal: At the time Jiangnan's prefectures and counties also debated relocating people into the Pass, alarming near and far.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Jiangnan's prefectures and counties also debated relocating people into the Pass, alarming near and far.

sentences.zh: 饒州吳世華起兵為亂，生臠縣令，啖其肉。

translations.literal: Wu Shihua of Raozhou raised troops in rebellion, cut the county magistrate alive into pieces, and ate his flesh.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shihua of Raozhou raised troops in rebellion, cut the county magistrate alive into pieces, and ate his flesh.

sentences.zh: 於是舊陳率土畢反，執長吏，抽其腸而殺之，曰：「更使儂誦五教邪！」

translations.literal: Thereupon all the old Chen lands rose in revolt; they seized chief officials, drew out their intestines and killed them, saying: "Are you going to make us recite the Five Teachings again!"
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon all the old Chen lands rose in revolt; they seized chief officials, drew out their intestines and killed them, saying: "Are you going to make us recite the Five Teachings again!"

sentences.zh: 尋詔內史令楊素討平之。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward an edict ordered Palace Director Yang Su to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward an edict ordered Palace Director Yang Su to suppress and pacify them.

sentences.zh: 時突厥都藍可汗屢為患，復令威至可汗所。

translations.literal: At the time the Turkic Khan Dulan repeatedly caused trouble, and Wei was again sent to the khan's court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Turkic Khan Dulan repeatedly caused trouble, and Wei was again sent to the khan's court.

sentences.zh: 威子夔以公子盛名，引致賓客，四海士大夫多歸之。

translations.literal: Wei's son Kui, famous as a minister's son, drew guests to him; scholars and officials from across the realm mostly rallied to him.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Kui, famous as a minister's son, drew guests to him; scholars and officials from across the realm mostly rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 時議樂，夔與國子博士何妥各有所持。

translations.literal: At the time when music was debated, Kui and Academician He Tuo of the Imperial Academy each held their own views.
translations.idiomatic: At the time when music was debated, Kui and Academician He Tuo of the Imperial Academy each held their own views.

sentences.zh: 於是夔、妥各為一議，使百僚署其所同。

translations.literal: Kui and Tuo each made one proposal and had the hundred officials sign which they agreed with.
translations.idiomatic: Kui and Tuo each made one proposal and had the hundred officials sign which they agreed with.

sentences.zh: 朝廷多附威，同夔者十八九。

translations.literal: The court mostly sided with Wei; eight or nine out of ten agreed with Kui.
translations.idiomatic: The court mostly sided with Wei; eight or nine out of ten agreed with Kui.

sentences.zh: 妥恚曰：「吾席間函丈四十餘年，反為昨暮兒之所屈也！」

translations.literal: Tuo said in anger: "I have lectured at the master's mat for more than forty years, yet I am defeated by a boy of yesterday!"
translations.idiomatic: Tuo said in anger: "I have lectured at the master's mat for more than forty years, yet I am defeated by a boy of yesterday!"

sentences.zh: 遂奏威與禮部尚書盧愷、吏部侍郎薛道衡、尚書右丞王弘、考功侍郎李同和等為朋黨，省中呼王弘為世子，李同和為叔，言二人如威子弟。

translations.literal: He then memorialized that Wei together with Director of Rites Lu Kai, Vice Director of Personnel Xue Daoheng, Vice Director of the Right Wang Hong, and Vice Director of Merit Li Tonghe formed a faction; within the Secretariat Wang Hong was called "heir" and Li Tonghe "uncle," saying the two were like Wei's sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized that Wei together with Director of Rites Lu Kai, Vice Director of Personnel Xue Daoheng, Vice Director of the Right Wang Hong, and Vice Director of Merit Li Tonghe formed a faction; within the Secretariat Wang Hong was called "heir" and Li Tonghe "uncle," saying the two were like Wei's sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 復言威以曲道任其從父弟徹、肅等罔冒為官。

translations.literal: He further said Wei used improper means to appoint his younger cousins by marriage Che and Su and others to office by false pretense.
translations.idiomatic: He further said Wei used improper means to appoint his younger cousins by marriage Che and Su and others to office by false pretense.

sentences.zh: 又國子學請黎陽人王孝逸為書學博士，威屬盧愷，以為其府參軍。

translations.literal: Also, when the Imperial Academy requested Wang Xiaoyi of Liyang as Doctor of Calligraphy, Wei asked Lu Kai to make him a staff officer in his office.
translations.idiomatic: Also, when the Imperial Academy requested Wang Xiaoyi of Liyang as Doctor of Calligraphy, Wei asked Lu Kai to make him a staff officer in his office.

sentences.zh: 上令蜀王秀、上柱國虞慶則等雜按之，事皆驗。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Prince Xiu of Shu, Pillar of State Yu Qingze, and others jointly to investigate; all the charges were verified.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Prince Xiu of Shu, Pillar of State Yu Qingze, and others jointly to investigate; all the charges were verified.

sentences.zh: 帝以宋書謝晦傳中朋黨事令威讀之。

translations.literal: The emperor had Wei read the account of factionalism in the biography of Xie Hui in the History of Song.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had Wei read the account of factionalism in the biography of Xie Hui in the History of Song.

sentences.zh: 威懼，免冠頓首。

translations.literal: Wei was afraid; he removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was afraid; he removed his cap and knocked his head on the ground.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「謝已晚矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Apology comes too late!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Apology comes too late!"

sentences.zh: 於是免威官爵，以開府就第。

translations.literal: Wei was then stripped of office and rank and sent home as Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Wei was then stripped of office and rank and sent home as Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 知名之士，坐威得罪者百餘人。

translations.literal: More than a hundred noted men were punished on account of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred noted men were punished on account of Wei.

sentences.zh: 未幾，帝曰：「蘇威德行者，但為人誤耳。」

translations.literal: Before long the emperor said: "Su Wei is a man of virtue—he was only misled by others."
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor said: "Su Wei is a man of virtue—he was only misled by others."

sentences.zh: 命之通籍。

translations.literal: He ordered him restored to court registry.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him restored to court registry.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復爵邳公，拜納言。

translations.literal: After more than a year his title as Duke of Pi was restored and he was appointed Palace Director.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year his title as Duke of Pi was restored and he was appointed Palace Director.

sentences.zh: 從祠太山，坐不敬免。

translations.literal: When accompanying the sacrifice at Mount Tai he was dismissed for disrespect.
translations.idiomatic: When accompanying the sacrifice at Mount Tai he was dismissed for disrespect.

sentences.zh: 俄而復位。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he was restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was restored to office.

sentences.zh: 帝謂群臣曰：「世人言蘇威詐清，家累金玉，此妄言也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to the ministers: "People say Su Wei feigns purity while his house is piled with gold and jade—this is false talk.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to the ministers: "People say Su Wei feigns purity while his house is piled with gold and jade—this is false talk.

sentences.zh: 然其性狠戾，不切世要，求名太甚，從己則悅，違之必怒，此其大病耳。」

translations.literal: Yet his nature is harsh and perverse, he does not grasp what the age requires, he seeks fame too much, is pleased when others follow him and must grow angry when they oppose him—this is his great flaw."
translations.idiomatic: Yet his nature is harsh and perverse, he does not grasp what the age requires, he seeks fame too much, is pleased when others follow him and must grow angry when they oppose him—this is his great flaw."

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，復拜尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: At the start of the Renshou era he was again appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Renshou era he was again appointed Vice Director of the Right of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝幸仁壽宮，以威總留事。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Renshou Palace, Wei was left to oversee all affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Renshou Palace, Wei was left to oversee all affairs.

sentences.zh: 及帝還，御史奏威職事多不理。

translations.literal: When the emperor returned, the censor memorialized that Wei had left many duties unhandled.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, the censor memorialized that Wei had left many duties unhandled.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，詰責威。
