translations.literal: The emperor was angry and interrogated and rebuked Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and interrogated and rebuked Wei.

sentences.zh: 威謝，帝亦止。

translations.literal: Wei apologized and the emperor also stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Wei apologized and the emperor also stopped.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，上將大起長城之役，威諫止之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was about to launch the great Great Wall project; Wei remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was about to launch the great Great Wall project; Wei remonstrated to stop it.

sentences.zh: 高熲、賀若弼之誅也，威坐相連免官。

translations.literal: When Gao Jiong and He Ruo were executed, Wei was implicated and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Jiong and He Ruo were executed, Wei was implicated and dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，拜魯郡太守，修羽儀。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Prefect of Lu Commandery with full ceremonial escort.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he was appointed Prefect of Lu Commandery with full ceremonial escort.

sentences.zh: 召拜太常卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，進拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: On campaign against Tuyuhun he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign against Tuyuhun he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，復為納言，與左翊衛大將軍宇文述、黃門侍郎裴矩、御史大夫裴蘊、內史侍郎虞世基參掌朝政，時人稱為五貴。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again became Palace Director and with Left Guard General Yuwen Shu, Palace Attendant Pei Ju, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, and Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji jointly managed court governance—people of the time called them the Five Nobles.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year he again became Palace Director and with Left Guard General Yuwen Shu, Palace Attendant Pei Ju, Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, and Secretariat Vice Director Yu Shiji jointly managed court governance—people of the time called them the Five Nobles.

sentences.zh: 及征遼東，以本官領右武衛大將軍，進位光祿大夫，賜爵房陵侯，尋進封房公。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign he retained his original post while leading the Right Martial Guard General, was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangling, and soon raised to Duke of Fang.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he retained his original post while leading the Right Martial Guard General, was advanced to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, enfeoffed as Marquis of Fangling, and soon raised to Duke of Fang.

sentences.zh: 以年老乞骸骨，不許。

translations.literal: On grounds of old age he requested to retire with his bones; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On grounds of old age he requested to retire with his bones; permission was not granted.

sentences.zh: 復以本官參掌選事。

translations.literal: He again participated in managing selection affairs in his original post.
translations.idiomatic: He again participated in managing selection affairs in his original post.

sentences.zh: 明年，從征遼東，領右禦衛大將軍。

translations.literal: The next year he followed the Liaodong campaign as Right Imperial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he followed the Liaodong campaign as Right Imperial Guard General.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感之反，帝引威於帳中，懼見於色，謂曰：「此小兒聰明，得不為患邪？」

translations.literal: When Yang Xuan'gan rebelled, the emperor drew Wei into his tent, fear showing on his face, and said: "This boy is clever—could he not become a threat?"
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuan'gan rebelled, the emperor drew Wei into his tent, fear showing on his face, and said: "This boy is clever—could he not become a threat?"

sentences.zh: 威曰：「粗疏非聰明者，必無慮，但恐浸成亂階耳。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "One who is crude and careless is not truly clever and surely need not be feared—but I fear he may gradually become a step toward chaos."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "One who is crude and careless is not truly clever and surely need not be feared—but I fear he may gradually become a step toward chaos."

sentences.zh: 威見勞役不已，百姓思亂，以此微欲諷帝。

translations.literal: Wei saw corvée labor unending and the people thinking of rebellion; by this he subtly wished to admonish the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Wei saw corvée labor unending and the people thinking of rebellion; by this he subtly wished to admonish the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝竟不悟。

translations.literal: The emperor ultimately did not understand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ultimately did not understand.

sentences.zh: 從還，至涿郡，詔威安撫關中，以其孫尚輦直長儇副。

translations.literal: On returning from the campaign, at Zhuo Commandery an edict ordered Wei to pacify Guanzhong, with his grandson Palace Escort Chief Xuan as assistant.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the campaign, at Zhuo Commandery an edict ordered Wei to pacify Guanzhong, with his grandson Palace Escort Chief Xuan as assistant.

sentences.zh: 威子鴻臚少卿夔先為關中簡黜大使。

translations.literal: Wei's son Kui, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, had already served as envoy for selection and dismissal in Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Wei's son Kui, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, had already served as envoy for selection and dismissal in Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 一家三人，俱使關右，三輔榮之。

translations.literal: Three men of one family were all sent to the west of the Pass—the Three Metropolises counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: Three men of one family were all sent to the west of the Pass—the Three Metropolises counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，帝手詔曰：「玉以潔潤，丹紫莫能渝其質；

translations.literal: After more than a year the emperor wrote by hand: "Jade is pure and moist—cinnabar and purple cannot alter its substance;
translations.idiomatic: After more than a year the emperor wrote by hand: "Jade is pure and moist—cinnabar and purple cannot alter its substance;

sentences.zh: 松表歲寒，霜尋莫能凋其采。

translations.literal: the pine shows the year's cold—frost and search cannot wither its hue.
translations.idiomatic: the pine shows the year's cold—frost cannot wither its hue.

sentences.zh: 可謂溫仁勁直，性之然乎。

translations.literal: One may call this gentle benevolence and firm uprightness—the nature of the man, is it not so?
translations.idiomatic: One may call this gentle benevolence and firm uprightness—the nature of the man, is it not so?

sentences.zh: 房公威，先後舊臣，朝之宿齒，棟樑社稷，弼諧朕躬，守文奉法，卑身率禮。

translations.literal: Duke of Fang Wei, old minister through successive reigns, senior elder of the court, pillar and beam of the altars of soil and grain, harmonizing assistant to my person, upholding culture and observing law, humbling himself and leading in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Fang Wei, old minister through successive reigns, senior elder of the court, pillar and beam of the altars of soil and grain, harmonizing assistant to my person, upholding culture and observing law, humbling himself and leading in ritual.

sentences.zh: 昔漢之三傑，輔惠帝者蕭何；

translations.literal: Of old among Han's Three Outstanding Men, Xiao He assisted Emperor Hui;
translations.idiomatic: Of old among Han's Three Outstanding Men, Xiao He assisted Emperor Hui;

sentences.zh: 周之十亂，佐成王者邵奭。

translations.literal: among Zhou's Ten Disruptors who aided the king, Shao Shi helped King Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: among Zhou's Ten Disruptors who aided the king, Shao Shi helped King Cheng.

sentences.zh: 國之寶器，其在得賢。

translations.literal: The state's precious vessel lies in obtaining the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: The state's precious vessel lies in obtaining the worthy.

sentences.zh: 參璟臺階，具瞻斯允。

translations.literal: He shares the jade steps of the terrace; all look to him with approval.
translations.idiomatic: He shares the jade steps of the terrace; all look to him with approval.

sentences.zh: 雖事藉論道，終期獻替，銓衡時和，朝寄為重。

translations.literal: Though affairs rely on discourse on the Way, in the end he is expected to offer correction; he weighs and balances the harmony of the times—the court's trust in him is weighty.
translations.idiomatic: Though affairs rely on discourse on the Way, in the end he is expected to offer correction; he weighs and balances the harmony of the times—the court's trust in him is weighty.

sentences.zh: 可開府儀同三司，餘並如故。」

translations.literal: He may be made Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers; all else remains as before."
translations.idiomatic: He may be made Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers; all else remains as before."

sentences.zh: 威當時尊重，朝臣莫與為比。

translations.literal: At the time Wei was held in such esteem that no court minister could compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Wei was held in such esteem that no court minister could compare with him.

sentences.zh: 後從幸雁門。

translations.literal: Later he accompanied the emperor to Yanmen.
translations.idiomatic: Later he accompanied the emperor to Yanmen.

sentences.zh: 為突厥所圍，朝廷危懼。

translations.literal: They were surrounded by the Turks and the court was filled with dread.
translations.idiomatic: They were surrounded by the Turks and the court was filled with dread.

sentences.zh: 帝欲輕騎潰圍而出。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to break out with a light cavalry force.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to break out with a light cavalry force.

sentences.zh: 威諫曰：「城守則我有餘力，輕騎則彼之所長。

translations.literal: Wei remonstrated: "If we hold the city we have surplus strength; light cavalry is what they excel at.
translations.idiomatic: Wei remonstrated: "If we hold the city we have surplus strength; light cavalry is what they excel at.

sentences.zh: 陛下萬乘主，何宜輕脫！」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is lord of ten thousand chariots—how can you lightly expose yourself!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is lord of ten thousand chariots—how can you lightly expose yourself!"

sentences.zh: 帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 突厥俄亦解圍去。

translations.literal: The Turks soon lifted the siege and departed.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks soon lifted the siege and departed.

sentences.zh: 車駕次太原，威以盜賊不止，勸帝還京師，深根固本，為社稷計。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage halted at Taiyuan, Wei, because bandits did not cease, urged the emperor to return to the capital, deepen roots and solidify the foundation, and plan for the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage halted at Taiyuan, Wei, because bandits did not cease, urged the emperor to return to the capital, deepen roots and solidify the foundation, and plan for the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 帝初從之，竟用宇文述等議，遂往東都。

translations.literal: The emperor at first agreed but ultimately followed Yuwen Shu and others' advice and went on to the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor at first agreed but ultimately followed Yuwen Shu and others' advice and went on to the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 天下大亂，威知帝不可匡正，甚患之。

translations.literal: The realm fell into great chaos; Wei knew the emperor could not be set right and was deeply troubled.
translations.idiomatic: The realm fell into great chaos; Wei knew the emperor could not be set right and was deeply troubled.

sentences.zh: 屬帝問盜賊事。

translations.literal: When the emperor asked about bandits,
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor asked about bandits,

sentences.zh: 宇文述曰：「盜賊信少，不足為虞。」

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu said: "Bandits are truly few—not enough to worry about."
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu said: "Bandits are truly few—not enough to worry about."

sentences.zh: 威不能詭對，以身隱殿柱。

translations.literal: Wei could not answer deceitfully and hid himself behind a hall pillar.
translations.idiomatic: Wei could not answer deceitfully and hid himself behind a hall pillar.

sentences.zh: 帝呼問之。

translations.literal: The emperor called and questioned him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor called and questioned him.

sentences.zh: 威曰：「臣非職司，不知多少，但患其漸近。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "I am not in charge of this office and do not know the numbers, but I worry that they are gradually drawing near."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "I am not in charge of this office and do not know the numbers, but I worry that they are gradually drawing near."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「何謂也？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What do you mean?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 威曰：「他日賊據長白山，今者近在滎陽、汜水。」

translations.literal: Wei said: "In former days bandits held Changbai Mountain; now they are close at Xingyang and Sishui."
translations.idiomatic: Wei said: "In former days bandits held Changbai Mountain; now they are close at Xingyang and Sishui."

sentences.zh: 帝不悅而罷。

translations.literal: The emperor was displeased and dismissed the session.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased and dismissed the session.

sentences.zh: 屬五月五日，百僚上饋，多以珍玩，威獻尚書一部，微以諷帝。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of the fifth month the hundred officials presented gifts, mostly rare curios; Wei offered one copy of the Documents and subtly wished to admonish the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth day of the fifth month the hundred officials presented gifts, mostly rare curios; Wei offered one copy of the Documents and subtly wished to admonish the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝彌不平。

translations.literal: The emperor was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was all the more displeased.

sentences.zh: 後復問伐遼東事，威對顧赦群盜，遣討高麗，帝益怒。

translations.literal: Later when he again asked about the Liaodong campaign, Wei answered by wishing to pardon all bandits and send them against Goguryeo; the emperor grew angrier still.
translations.idiomatic: Later when he again asked about the Liaodong campaign, Wei answered by wishing to pardon all bandits and send them against Goguryeo; the emperor grew angrier still.

sentences.zh: 御史大夫輩蘊希旨，令御史張行本，奏威昔在高陽典選，濫授人官，怯畏突厥，請還京師。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, seeking to please the emperor's intent, had Censor Zhang Xingben memorialize that Wei, when managing selection at Gaoyang, had wantonly granted offices, feared the Turks, and asked to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, seeking to please the emperor's intent, had Censor Zhang Xingben memorialize that Wei, when managing selection at Gaoyang, had wantonly granted offices, feared the Turks, and asked to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 帝令案其事，乃下詔曰：「威立性朋黨，好異端，懷挾詭道，徼幸名利，詆訶律令，謗訕台省。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the matter investigated and then issued an edict: "Wei by nature forms factions, loves heterodox ways, harbors crooked doctrines, seeks fame and profit by chance, slanders statutes and commands, and reviles the Secretariat and provinces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the matter investigated and then issued an edict: "Wei by nature forms factions, loves heterodox ways, harbors crooked doctrines, seeks fame and profit by chance, slanders statutes and commands, and reviles the Secretariat and provinces.

sentences.zh: 昔歲薄伐，奉述先志，凡預切問，各盡胸臆，而威不以開懷，遂無對命。

translations.literal: Last year on the brief campaign, carrying out the former intent, all who were closely questioned should have fully expressed their hearts—but Wei did not open his heart and therefore gave no answer to the charge.
translations.idiomatic: Last year on the brief campaign, carrying out the former intent, all who were closely questioned should have fully expressed their hearts—but Wei did not open his heart and therefore gave no answer to the charge.

sentences.zh: 啟沃之道，其若是乎！」

translations.literal: Is this how the way of counsel and nourishment should be!"
translations.idiomatic: Is this how the way of counsel and nourishment should be!"

sentences.zh: 於是除名。

translations.literal: He was then struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was then struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後月餘，人有奏威與突厥陰圖不軌。

translations.literal: More than a month later someone memorialized that Wei secretly plotted treason with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: More than a month later someone memorialized that Wei secretly plotted treason with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 大理簿責威。

translations.literal: The Court of Justice registered charges against Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Justice registered charges against Wei.

sentences.zh: 威自陳精誠不能上感，瑕爨屢彰，罪當萬死。

translations.literal: Wei stated himself that his sincerity could not move those above, his faults repeatedly appeared, and his crime deserved ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stated himself that his sincerity could not move those above, his faults repeatedly appeared, and his crime deserved ten thousand deaths.

sentences.zh: 帝憫而釋之。

translations.literal: The emperor took pity and released him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity and released him.

sentences.zh: 其年，從幸江都宮。

translations.literal: That year he accompanied the emperor to the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: That year he accompanied the emperor to the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 帝將復用威，裴蘊、虞世基奏言昏耄贏疾，帝乃止。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to employ Wei again, but Pei Yun and Yu Shiji memorialized that he was senile, frail, and ill, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was about to employ Wei again, but Pei Yun and Yu Shiji memorialized that he was senile, frail, and ill, and the emperor then stopped.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆，以威為光祿大夫、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he made Wei Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he made Wei Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers.

sentences.zh: 化及敗，歸於李密。

translations.literal: When Huaji was defeated, Wei went over to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji was defeated, Wei went over to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密敗，歸東都，越王侗以為上柱國、邳公。

translations.literal: When Mi was defeated, Wei returned to the Eastern Capital; Prince of Yue Tong made him Pillar of State and Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Mi was defeated, Wei returned to the Eastern Capital; Prince of Yue Tong made him Pillar of State and Duke of Pi.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，署太師。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he appointed Wei Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he appointed Wei Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 威自以隋室舊臣，遭逢喪亂，所經之處，皆與時消息，以求容免。

translations.literal: Wei considered himself an old minister of Sui who had met chaos and ruin; wherever he passed he adapted to the times to seek safety and exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Wei considered himself an old minister of Sui who had met chaos and ruin; wherever he passed he adapted to the times to seek safety and exemption.

sentences.zh: 及太宗平世充，坐於東都閶闔門內，威請謁見，稱老病不能拜起。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong pacified Shichong, Wei sat inside the Changhe Gate of the Eastern Capital and requested an audience, saying he was old and ill and could not bow and rise.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong pacified Shichong, Wei sat inside the Changhe Gate of the Eastern Capital and requested an audience, saying he was old and ill and could not bow and rise.

sentences.zh: 上遣人數之曰：「公隋朝宰輔，政亂不能匡救，遂令品物塗炭，君弑國亡。

translations.literal: The emperor sent someone to rebuke him: "You were chief minister of Sui; when governance was chaotic you could not set it right, until all things were scorched, the ruler murdered and the state destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent someone to rebuke him: "You were chief minister of Sui; when governance was chaotic you could not set it right, until all things were scorched, the ruler murdered and the state destroyed.

sentences.zh: 見李密、世充皆拜伏舞蹈。

translations.literal: Before Li Mi and Shichong you all bowed prostrate and danced in obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Before Li Mi and Shichong you all bowed prostrate and danced in obeisance.

sentences.zh: 今既老病，無勞相見。」

translations.literal: Now that you are old and ill, there is no need for us to meet.
translations.idiomatic: Now that you are old and ill, there is no need for us to meet.

sentences.zh: 尋入長安，至朝堂請見，高祖又不許。

translations.literal: Soon he entered Chang'an and came to the court hall requesting an audience, but Emperor Gaozu again refused.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he entered Chang'an and came to the court hall requesting an audience, but Emperor Gaozu again refused.

sentences.zh: 終於家，時年八十二。

translations.literal: He died at home at the age of eighty-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of eighty-two.

sentences.zh: 威行己清儉，以廉慎見稱。

translations.literal: Wei in conduct was pure and frugal and was praised for integrity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Wei in conduct was pure and frugal and was praised for integrity and caution.

sentences.zh: 然每至公議，惡人異已，雖或小事，必固爭之。

translations.literal: Yet whenever there was public discussion he hated those who differed from him; even over small matters he had to argue stubbornly.
translations.idiomatic: Yet whenever there was public discussion he hated those who differed from him; even over small matters he had to argue stubbornly.

sentences.zh: 時人以為無大臣之體。

translations.literal: People of the time thought he lacked the bearing of a great minister.
translations.idiomatic: People of the time thought he lacked the bearing of a great minister.

sentences.zh: 所修格令章程，並行於當世，頗傷煩碎，論者以為非簡久之法。

translations.literal: The codes, commands, forms, and regulations he compiled all operated in his age but were rather burdensome and fragmented; commentators thought them not a simple and enduring law.
translations.idiomatic: The codes, commands, forms, and regulations he compiled all operated in his age but were rather burdensome and fragmented; commentators thought them not a simple and enduring law.

sentences.zh: 及大業末年，尤多征役，至於論功行賞，威每承望風旨，輒寢其事。

translations.literal: By the late Daye era corvée and service were especially numerous; when merit was discussed and rewards granted, Wei always watched the prevailing intent and then shelved the matter.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Daye era corvée and service were especially numerous; when merit was discussed and rewards granted, Wei always watched the prevailing intent and then shelved the matter.

sentences.zh: 時群盜蜂起，郡縣有奏聞者，又訶詰使人，令減賊數，故出師攻討，多不克捷。

translations.literal: When bandits rose everywhere and commanderies and counties reported them, he again interrogated and rebuked the messengers and ordered the bandit count reduced; therefore when armies went out to attack, they often did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose everywhere and commanderies and counties reported them, he again interrogated and rebuked the messengers and ordered the bandit count reduced; therefore when armies went out to attack, they often did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 由是遂致敗亂，為物議所譏。

translations.literal: By this defeat and chaos were brought about, and he was ridiculed in public opinion.
translations.idiomatic: By this defeat and chaos were brought about, and he was ridiculed in public opinion.

sentences.zh: 子夔。

translations.literal: His son was Kui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Kui.

sentences.zh: 夔字伯尼。

translations.literal: Kui, courtesy name Boni.
translations.idiomatic: Kui, courtesy name Boni.

sentences.zh: 聰敏有口辯，然性輕險無行。

translations.literal: He was clever and quick with speech and debate, yet by nature he was frivolous, rash, and without proper conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He was clever and quick with speech and debate, yet by nature he was frivolous, rash, and without proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 八歲誦詩，兼解騎射。

translations.literal: At eight he could recite poetry and also understood riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: At eight he could recite poetry and also understood riding and archery.

sentences.zh: 年十三，從父至尚書省。

translations.literal: At thirteen he followed his father to the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At thirteen he followed his father to the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 與安德王雄射，賭得駿馬而歸。

translations.literal: He shot arrows with Prince Xiong of Ande in a wager and won a fine horse to take home.
translations.idiomatic: He shot arrows with Prince Xiong of Ande in a wager and won a fine horse to take home.

sentences.zh: 十四詣學，與諸儒議論，詞致可觀。

translations.literal: At fourteen he went to the academy and debated with the Confucian scholars; his words and expression were admirable.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he went to the academy and debated with the Confucian scholars; his words and expression were admirable.

sentences.zh: 見者皆稱善。

translations.literal: All who saw this praised him.
translations.idiomatic: All who saw this praised him.

sentences.zh: 及長，博覽群言，尤以鍾律自命。

translations.literal: When grown he read widely among books and especially styled himself an authority on pitch pipes and scales.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he read widely among books and especially styled himself an authority on pitch pipes and scales.

sentences.zh: 初名哲，字知人，父威由是改之，頗為有識所哂，起家太子通事舍人。

translations.literal: His original name was Zhe, courtesy name Zhiren; his father Wei changed them on this account, and men of discernment rather mocked this; he began his career as Palace Attendant of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: His original name was Zhe, courtesy name Zhiren; his father Wei changed them on this account, and men of discernment rather mocked this; he began his career as Palace Attendant of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 楊素見而奇之，每戲威曰：「楊素無兒，蘇夔無父。」

translations.literal: Yang Su saw him and marveled; he often joked with Wei: "Yang Su has no son; Su Kui has no father.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su saw him and marveled; he often joked with Wei: "Yang Su has no son; Su Kui has no father.

sentences.zh: 後與鄭譯、何舀議樂，得罪，議寢不行。

translations.literal: Later he debated music with Zheng Yi and He Yao, gave offense, and the proposal was shelved and not implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Later he debated music with Zheng Yi and He Yao, gave offense, and the proposal was shelved and never implemented.

sentences.zh: 著樂志十五篇以見其志。

translations.literal: He wrote fifteen chapters of Music Records to show his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote fifteen chapters of Music Records to show his intent.

sentences.zh: 數載，遷太子舍人，以罪免居數年。

translations.literal: After several years he was transferred to Attendant of the Crown Prince; because of an offense he was dismissed and lived at home for several years.
translations.idiomatic: After several years he was transferred to Attendant of the Crown Prince; because of an offense he was dismissed and lived at home for several years.

sentences.zh: 仁壽三年，詔天下舉達禮樂源者。

translations.literal: In the third year of Renshou an edict ordered the realm to recommend those who had mastered the sources of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Renshou an edict ordered the realm to recommend those who had mastered the sources of ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 晉王昭時為雍州牧，舉夔。

translations.literal: Prince of Jin Zhao, then Governor of Yongzhou, recommended Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Jin Zhao, then Governor of Yongzhou, recommended Kui.

sentences.zh: 與諸州所舉五十餘人謁見。

translations.literal: He presented himself at audience together with more than fifty others recommended by the various provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He presented himself at audience together with more than fifty others recommended by the various provinces.

sentences.zh: 帝望夔，謂侍臣曰：「唯此一人，稱吾所舉。」

translations.literal: The emperor looked at Kui and said to his attendants: "Only this one man fits what I recommended.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor looked at Kui and said to his attendants: "Only this one man fits what I recommended.

sentences.zh: 於是拜晉王友。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Companion to the Prince of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Companion to the Prince of Jin.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，曆太子洗馬、司朝謁者。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded he served successively as Groom of the Crown Prince and Director of Court Audiences.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang succeeded he served successively as Groom of the Crown Prince and Director of Court Audiences.

sentences.zh: 以父免職，夔亦去官。

translations.literal: When his father was dismissed from office, Kui also left his post.
translations.idiomatic: When his father was dismissed from office, Kui also left his post.

sentences.zh: 後曆尚書職方郎、燕王司馬。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Director of Territories in the Imperial Secretariat and Marshal to the Prince of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served successively as Director of Territories in the Imperial Secretariat and Marshal to the Prince of Yan.

sentences.zh: 遼東之役，以功拜朝散大夫。

translations.literal: On the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Grand Master of Dispersal for merit.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he was appointed Grand Master of Dispersal for merit.

sentences.zh: 時帝方勤遠略，蠻夷來朝。

translations.literal: At the time the emperor was pressing distant strategy and barbarians came to court.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the emperor was pressing distant strategy and barbarians came to court.

sentences.zh: 帝謂宇文述、虞世基曰：「四夷率服，觀禮華夏，鴻臚之職，須歸令望。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Yuwen Shu and Yu Shiji: "The four barbarians all submit and come to observe ritual in the heartland; the office of the Court of Imperial Entertainments requires a man of fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Yuwen Shu and Yu Shiji: "The four barbarians all submit and come to observe ritual in the heartland; the office of the Court of Imperial Entertainments requires a man of fine reputation.

sentences.zh: 甯有多才藝美容儀，可接賓客者為之乎？」

translations.literal: Is there one with many talents, skills, and fine appearance who can receive guests for the post?
translations.idiomatic: Is there one with many talents, skills, and fine appearance who can receive guests for the post?

sentences.zh: 威以夔對。

translations.literal: Wei named Kui.
translations.idiomatic: Wei recommended Kui.

sentences.zh: 即日拜鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: That same day Kui was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Kui was appointed Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.

sentences.zh: 其年，高昌王麹伯雅來朝，朝廷妻以公主。

translations.literal: That year King Qu Boya of Gaochang came to court and the court gave him a princess in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: That year King Qu Boya of Gaochang came to court and the court gave him a princess in marriage.

sentences.zh: 夔有雅望，令主婚。

translations.literal: Kui had a fine reputation and was ordered to preside over the marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Kui had a fine reputation and was ordered to preside over the marriage.

sentences.zh: 其後延安、弘化等數郡盜賊屯結，詔夔巡關中。

translations.literal: Afterward bandits gathered in several commanderies including Yan'an and Honghua; an edict ordered Kui to tour Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward bandits gathered in several commanderies including Yan'an and Honghua; an edict ordered Kui to tour Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 及突厥圍雁門，夔于鎮城東南為弩樓、車箱、獸圈，一夕而就。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, Kui built crossbow towers, wagon boxes, and animal pens southeast of the garrison town—all in one night.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, Kui built crossbow towers, wagon boxes, and animal pens southeast of the garrison town—all in one night.

sentences.zh: 帝見善之。

translations.literal: The emperor saw this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor saw this and approved.

sentences.zh: 以功進位通議大夫。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Universal Discussion.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was advanced to Grand Master of Universal Discussion.

sentences.zh: 坐父事，除名。

translations.literal: Because of his father's affair he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's affair he was struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 後會丁母憂，不勝哀，卒，時年四十九。

translations.literal: Later, while observing mourning for his mother, he could not bear the grief and died at the age of forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Later, while observing mourning for his mother, he could not bear the grief and died at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 綽弟椿，字令欽。

translations.literal: Chuo's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Lingqin.
translations.idiomatic: Chuo's younger brother Chun, courtesy name Lingqin.

sentences.zh: 性廉慎，沈勇有決斷。

translations.literal: By nature he was incorrupt and cautious, steady and brave with decisive judgment.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was incorrupt and cautious, steady and brave with decisive judgment.

sentences.zh: 魏正光中，關右賊亂，椿應募討之，授蕩寇將軍。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when bandits rebelled west of the Pass, Chun answered the recruitment to suppress them and was appointed General Who Pacifies Bandits.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguang era of Wei, when bandits rebelled west of the Pass, Chun answered the recruitment to suppress them and was appointed General Who Pacifies Bandits.

sentences.zh: 以功累遷中散大夫，賜爵美陽子。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he was promoted in succession to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Viscount of Meiyang.

sentences.zh: 大統初，拜鎮東將軍、金紫光祿大夫，賜姓賀蘭氏。

translations.literal: At the start of Datong he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and granted the surname Helan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Datong he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal, and granted the surname Helan.

sentences.zh: 後除帥都督，行弘農郡事。

translations.literal: Later he was made Commander-in-Chief and administered the affairs of Hongnong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was made Commander-in-Chief and administered the affairs of Hongnong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 椿當官強濟，特為周文帝所知。

translations.literal: Chun in office was forceful and effective and was especially known to Emperor Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chun in office was forceful and effective and was especially known to Emperor Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，置當州鄉師，自非鄉望允當眾心者不得預焉。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year local village chiefs were established; unless one was a village elder truly acceptable to the people's hearts one could not participate.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year local village chiefs were established; unless one was a village elder truly acceptable to the people's hearts one could not participate.

sentences.zh: 乃令驛追椿，領鄉兵。

translations.literal: They then sent a post station to summon Chun back and had him lead the village militia.
translations.idiomatic: They then sent a post station to summon Chun back and had him lead the village militia.

sentences.zh: 其年，破槃頭氏有功，除散騎常侍，加大都督。

translations.literal: That year, for merit in defeating the Pantou clan, he was made Regular Attendant and promoted to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: That year, for merit in defeating the Pantou clan, he was made Regular Attendant and promoted to Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 十六年，征隨郡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he campaigned against Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he campaigned against Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 軍還，除武功郡守。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was made Prefect of Wugong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned he was made Prefect of Wugong Commandery.

sentences.zh: 既為本邑，以清儉自居，小大之政，必盡忠恕。

translations.literal: Since it was his native district he lived in purity and frugality; in great and small governance he always exhausted loyalty and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: Since it was his native district he lived in purity and frugality; in great and small governance he always exhausted loyalty and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 進爵為侯，位驃騎大將軍、開府儀同三司、大都督。

translations.literal: He was advanced in rank to marquis and held the posts of General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced in rank to marquis and held the posts of General of Agile Cavalry, Grand Master of the Palace with Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Grand Commander.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子植嗣。

translations.literal: His son Zhi inherited his title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi inherited his title.

sentences.zh: 亮字景順，綽從兄也。

translations.literal: Liang, courtesy name Jingshun, was Chuo's older cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, courtesy name Jingshun, was Chuo's older cousin.

sentences.zh: 祖稚，字天佑，位中書侍郎、玉門郡守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi, courtesy name Tianyou, held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Yumen Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi, courtesy name Tianyou, held the posts of Vice Director of the Secretariat and Prefect of Yumen Commandery.

sentences.zh: 父祐，泰山郡守。

translations.literal: His father You was Prefect of Taishan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father You was Prefect of Taishan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 亮少通敏，博學好屬文，善章奏，與弟湛等皆著名西土，一家舉二秀才。

translations.literal: From youth Liang was quick and perceptive, broadly learned and fond of composition, skilled at memorials and reports; he and his younger brother Zhan and others were all famous in the western lands—one family produced two Recommended Scholars.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liang was quick and perceptive, broadly learned and fond of composition, skilled at memorials and reports; he and his younger brother Zhan and others were all famous in the western lands—one family produced two Recommended Scholars.

sentences.zh: 亮初舉秀才，至洛陽，過河內常景。

translations.literal: When Liang was first recommended as a scholar he went to Luoyang and passed through Henei to visit Chang Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang was first recommended as a scholar he went to Luoyang and passed through Henei to visit Chang Jing.

sentences.zh: 景深器之，而謂人曰：「秦中才學可以抗山東者，將此人乎」！

translations.literal: Jing greatly valued him and said to others: "Among the talent and learning of Qin that can match those of the eastern lands—is it this man!"
translations.idiomatic: Jing greatly valued him and said to others: "Among the talent and learning of Qin that can match those of the eastern lands—is it this man!"

sentences.zh: 魏齊王蕭寶夤引為參軍。

translations.literal: Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi of Wei, brought him in as a staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Baoyin, Prince of Qi of Wei, brought him in as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 寶夤遷大將軍，仍為之掾。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was transferred to Grand General, Liang still served as his aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was transferred to Grand General, Liang still served as his aide.

sentences.zh: 寶夤雅相知重，凡有文檄謀議，皆以委之。

translations.literal: Baoyin deeply knew and valued him; all documents, proclamations, and plans were entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin deeply knew and valued him; all documents, proclamations, and plans were entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 尋行武功郡事，甚著聲績。

translations.literal: Soon he administered the affairs of Wugong Commandery with notable reputation and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he administered the affairs of Wugong Commandery with notable reputation and achievement.

sentences.zh: 寶夤作亂，以亮為黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Baoyin rebelled, he made Liang Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin rebelled, he made Liang Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 亮善處人間，與物無忤。

translations.literal: Liang was skilled in dealing with people and gave no offense to others.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was skilled in dealing with people and gave no offense to others.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤敗，從之者多遇禍，唯亮獲全。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was defeated, many who followed him met disaster; only Liang escaped whole.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was defeated, many who followed him met disaster; only Liang escaped whole.

sentences.zh: 及長孫承業、爾硃天光等西討，並以亮為郎中，專典文翰。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Chengye, Erzhu Tianguang, and others campaigned west, all made Liang a Director and put him in charge of documents.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Chengye, Erzhu Tianguang, and others campaigned west, all made Liang a Director and put him in charge of documents.

sentences.zh: 賀拔岳為關西行台，引亮為左丞，典機密。

translations.literal: When Heba Yue was Grand Commissioner west of the Pass, he brought Liang in as Left Assistant Director in charge of secret affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Heba Yue was Grand Commissioner west of the Pass, he brought Liang in as Left Assistant Director in charge of secret affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏孝武西遷，遷吏部郎中。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Liang was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaowu of Wei moved west, Liang was transferred to Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大統二年，拜給事黃門侍郎，領中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he was appointed Attending Palace Attendant and concurrently Palace Attendant Drafting Documents.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he was appointed Attending Palace Attendant and concurrently Palace Attendant Drafting Documents.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝子宜都王式為秦州刺史，以亮為司馬。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei's son Prince Shi of Yidu was made Governor of Qinzhou and appointed Liang as Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei's son Prince Shi of Yidu was made Governor of Qinzhou and appointed Liang as Marshal.

sentences.zh: 帝謂亮曰：「黃門侍郎豈可為秦州司馬？

translations.literal: The emperor said to Liang: "How can a Palace Attendant serve as Marshal of Qinzhou?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Liang: "How can a Palace Attendant serve as Marshal of Qinzhou?

sentences.zh: 直以朕愛子出籓，故以心腹相委，勿以為恨。」

translations.literal: It is simply because I love my son and send him out to his fief that I entrust you as my trusted inner man—do not take it as a grievance.
translations.idiomatic: It is simply because I love my son and send him out to his fief that I entrust you as my trusted inner man—do not take it as a grievance.

sentences.zh: 臨辭，賜以御馬。

translations.literal: At parting he bestowed an imperial horse.
translations.idiomatic: At parting the emperor bestowed an imperial horse on him.

sentences.zh: 八年，封臨涇縣子，除中書監，領著作，修國史。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linjing, made Director of the Secretariat, concurrently head of the History Office, and charged with compiling the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Linjing, made Director of the Secretariat, concurrently head of the History Office, and charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 亮有機辯，善談笑。

translations.literal: Liang had quick wit and eloquence and was skilled at conversation and laughter.
translations.idiomatic: Liang had quick wit and eloquence and was skilled at conversation and laughter.

sentences.zh: 周文帝甚重之，有所籌議，率多會旨。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued him greatly; in deliberations he mostly hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou valued him greatly; in deliberations he mostly hit the mark.

sentences.zh: 記人之善，忘人之過，薦達後進，常如弗及，故當世敬慕。

translations.literal: He remembered people's virtues and forgot their faults, recommended and advanced the young, always as if he could not do enough—therefore his age revered and admired him.
translations.idiomatic: He remembered people's virtues and forgot their faults, recommended and advanced the young, always as if he could not do enough—therefore his age revered and admired him.

sentences.zh: 曆秘書監、大行台尚書，出為岐州刺史。

translations.literal: He served successively as Director of the Palace Library and Director of the Grand Commission Secretariat, then went out as Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as Director of the Palace Library and Director of the Grand Commission Secretariat, then went out as Governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以其作牧本州，特給路車、鼓吹，先還其宅，並給騎士三千，列習儀，遊鄉党，經過故人，歡飲旬日，然後入州。

translations.literal: Because the court made him governor of his native province, he was specially given a state carriage and musical escort, first returned to his house, and also given three thousand mounted guards; they drilled in ceremony, toured the villages, visited old friends, feasted joyfully for ten days, and only then entered the province.
translations.idiomatic: Because the court made him governor of his native province, he was specially given a state carriage and musical escort, first returned to his house, and also given three thousand mounted guards; they drilled in ceremony, toured the villages, visited old friends, feasted joyfully for ten days, and only then entered the province.

sentences.zh: 世以為榮。

translations.literal: The age considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: The age considered it an honor.

sentences.zh: 十七年，徵拜侍中，卒於位。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was summoned and appointed Palace Attendant; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈本官。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted his former office.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted the same office he had held.

sentences.zh: 亮少與從弟綽俱知名，然綽文章稍不逮亮，至於經畫進趣，亮又減之。

translations.literal: From youth Liang and his younger cousin Chuo were both famous, yet Chuo's literary compositions were somewhat inferior to Liang's; as for planning and forward progress, Liang was again the lesser.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Liang and his younger cousin Chuo were both renowned, yet Chuo's literary compositions fell somewhat short of Liang's, while in strategic planning and forward momentum Liang in turn fell short of Chuo.

sentences.zh: 故世稱二蘇焉。

translations.literal: Therefore the age called them the Two Sus.
translations.idiomatic: For this reason the age called them the Two Sus.

sentences.zh: 亮自大統以來，無歲不轉官，一年或至三遷。

translations.literal: From Datong onward Liang was transferred every year without exception; in a single year he might be promoted as many as three times.
translations.idiomatic: From the Datong era onward Liang was transferred every single year, and in one year he might be promoted as many as three times.

sentences.zh: 僉曰才至，不怪其速也。

translations.literal: All said his talent had arrived—they did not marvel at the speed.
translations.idiomatic: All agreed his talent had fully arrived, and no one found the pace surprising.

sentences.zh: 所著文筆數十篇，頗行於世。

translations.literal: The several dozen pieces of prose he wrote circulated widely in his age.
translations.idiomatic: The several dozen essays he wrote circulated widely in his time.

sentences.zh: 子師嗣，以亮名重于時，起家黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His son Shi inherited the title; because Liang's name weighed heavily in the age, Shi began his career as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shi inherited the title, and because Liang's name carried great weight in the age, Shi began his career as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 亮弟湛，字景俊。

translations.literal: Liang's younger brother Zhan, courtesy name Jingjun.
translations.idiomatic: Liang's younger brother Zhan, whose courtesy name was Jingjun.

sentences.zh: 少有志行，與亮俱著名西土。

translations.literal: From youth he had ambition and conduct; he and Liang were both famous in the western lands.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had ambition and integrity, and he and Liang were both famous in the western lands.

sentences.zh: 年二十餘，舉秀才，除奉朝請，領侍御史，加員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: In his twenties he was recommended as a scholar, appointed Responding Courtier, concurrently Regular Censor, with the additional post of Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties he was recommended as a Scholar, appointed Responding Courtier, made concurrent Regular Censor, and given the additional post of Supernumerary Attendant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 蕭寶夤西討，以湛為行台郎中，深見委任。

translations.literal: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, he made Zhan Director of the Grand Commission Secretariat and deeply entrusted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiao Baoyin campaigned west, he appointed Zhan Director of the Grand Commission Secretariat and deeply entrusted him.

sentences.zh: 及寶夤將謀叛逆，湛時臥疾於家。

translations.literal: When Baoyin was about to plot rebellion, Zhan was then ill abed at home.
translations.idiomatic: When Baoyin was about to plot rebellion, Zhan was confined to his bed at home by illness.

sentences.zh: 寶夤乃令湛從母弟天水姜儉謂湛曰：「吾不能坐受死亡，今便為身計，不復作魏臣也。

translations.literal: Baoyin had Zhan's maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui tell Zhan: "I cannot sit and await death; I shall now plan for myself and no longer serve as a minister of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin then had Zhan's maternal cousin Jiang Jian of Tianshui tell Zhan: "I cannot sit and wait for death; I must now plan for my own survival and will no longer serve as a minister of Wei.

sentences.zh: 與卿死生榮辱，方當共之，故以相報。」

translations.literal: Life and death, honor and disgrace with you—we should share them together; therefore I inform you thus.
translations.idiomatic: Life and death, honor and disgrace with you—we ought to share them together, and so I am telling you this.

sentences.zh: 湛聞之，舉聲大哭。

translations.literal: When Zhan heard this, he burst into loud weeping.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhan heard this, he broke into loud weeping.

sentences.zh: 儉遽止之曰：「何得便爾？」

translations.literal: Jian hastily stopped him: "How can you be like this at once?
translations.idiomatic: Jian hastily stopped him and said: "How can you react like this so suddenly?

sentences.zh: 湛曰：「闔門百口，即時屠滅，云何不哭！」

translations.literal: Zhan said: "My whole household of a hundred mouths will be slaughtered on the spot—how can I not weep!
translations.idiomatic: Zhan said: "My whole household of a hundred mouths will be slaughtered at once—how can I not weep!

sentences.zh: 哭數十聲，徐謂儉曰：「為我白齊王，王本以窮而歸人，賴朝廷假王羽翼，遂得榮寵至此。

translations.literal: After weeping dozens of times, he slowly told Jian: "Tell the Prince of Qi for me: the prince originally came to others in poverty; relying on the court to lend him wings, he attained glory and favor to this point.
translations.idiomatic: After weeping dozens of times, he slowly told Jian: "Tell the Prince of Qi for me: the prince originally came to others in destitution; relying on the court to lend him wings, he attained glory and favor to this point.

sentences.zh: 既屬國步多虞，不能竭誠報德，豈可乘人間隙，便有問鼎之心乎！

translations.literal: Now that the state faces many perils, you cannot exhaust your loyalty to repay grace—how can you seize upon a gap in affairs and harbor the heart to seize the throne!
translations.idiomatic: Now that the state faces many perils, you cannot exhaust your loyalty to repay grace—how can you seize upon a moment of weakness and harbor the heart to seize the throne!

sentences.zh: 今魏德雖衰，天命未改，王之恩義，未洽於人，破亡之期，必不旋踵。

translations.literal: Though Wei's virtue has waned, Heaven's mandate has not shifted; the prince's grace and righteousness have not reached the people; the day of ruin and destruction will surely come before he can turn.
translations.idiomatic: Though Wei's virtue has waned, Heaven's mandate has not changed; the prince's grace and righteousness have not won over the people; the day of ruin and destruction will surely come before he can turn around.

sentences.zh: 蘇湛終不能以積世忠貞之基，一旦為王族滅也。」

translations.literal: Su Zhan finally cannot, on foundations of loyalty across generations, in one day become destroyed with the princely clan.
translations.idiomatic: Su Zhan cannot, on foundations of loyalty built across generations, in a single day be destroyed together with the princely clan.

sentences.zh: 寶夤復令儉謂湛曰：「此是救命之計，不得不爾。」

translations.literal: Baoyin again had Jian tell Zhan: "This is a plan to save our lives—there is no choice but to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin again had Jian tell Zhan: "This is a plan to save our lives, and there is no choice but to do it.

sentences.zh: 湛復曰：「凡舉大事，當得天下奇士。

translations.literal: Zhan replied again: "Whenever one undertakes a great matter, one must obtain outstanding men of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan replied again: "Whenever one undertakes a great matter, one must obtain outstanding men from across the realm.

sentences.zh: 今但共長安博徒小兒輩為此計，豈有辦哉？

translations.literal: Now you only plan this together with gambling youths of Chang'an—how could it succeed?
translations.idiomatic: Now you only plan this together with gambling youths of Chang'an—how could it possibly succeed?

sentences.zh: 湛不忍見荊棘生王戶庭也。

translations.literal: Zhan cannot bear to see thorns grow in the prince's courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan cannot bear to see thorns growing in the prince's courtyard.

sentences.zh: 願賜骸骨還舊裏，庶歸全地下，無愧先人。」

translations.literal: I beg to be granted my bones and returned to my old home, that I may return whole beneath the earth and feel no shame before my ancestors.
translations.idiomatic: I beg to be granted my bones and sent back to my old home, that I may return whole beneath the earth and feel no shame before my ancestors.

sentences.zh: 寶夤素重之，知必不為已用，遂聽還武功。

translations.literal: Baoyin had always valued him, knew he would never serve his purpose, and therefore permitted him to return to Wugong.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin had always valued him, knew he would never serve his purpose, and therefore allowed him to return to Wugong.

sentences.zh: 寶夤後果敗。

translations.literal: Baoyin was indeed defeated afterward.
translations.idiomatic: Baoyin was later defeated, just as Zhan had foreseen.

sentences.zh: 孝莊帝即位，徵拜尚書郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaozhuang succeeded, Zhan was summoned and appointed Director in the Imperial Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaozhuang succeeded to the throne, Zhan was summoned and appointed Director in the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗謂之曰：「聞卿答蕭寶夤，甚有美辭，可為我說之。」

translations.literal: The emperor once said to him: "I hear your reply to Xiao Baoyin had fine words—tell them to me.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once said to him: "I hear your reply to Xiao Baoyin contained fine words—tell them to me.

sentences.zh: 湛頓首謝曰：「臣自惟言辭不如伍被遠矣，然始終不易，竊謂過之。

translations.literal: Zhan bowed his head and said: "I myself think my words fall far short of Wu Bei's, yet in holding firm from start to finish, I venture to say I surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan bowed his head and said: "I myself think my words fall far short of Wu Bei's, yet in holding firm from beginning to end, I dare say I surpassed him.

sentences.zh: 但臣與寶夤周旋契闊，言得盡心，而不能令其守節，此臣之罪也。」

translations.literal: But I moved among Baoyin in close association, spoke with full heart, yet could not make him keep his integrity—this is my offense.
translations.idiomatic: But I moved in close association with Baoyin and spoke with all my heart, yet could not make him keep his integrity—this is my offense.

sentences.zh: 孝莊大悅，加散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaozhuang was greatly pleased and added the post of Attendant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaozhuang was greatly pleased and promoted him to Attendant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 尋遷中書。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to the Central Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to the Central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 孝武初，以疾還鄉里，終於家。

translations.literal: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign, because of illness he returned to his native place and died at home.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he returned to his native place because of illness and died at home.

sentences.zh: 贈散騎常侍、鎮西將軍、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted Regular Attendant Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted Regular Attendant Cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and Governor of Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 湛弟讓，字景恕。

translations.literal: Zhan's younger brother Rang, courtesy name Jingshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan's younger brother Rang, whose courtesy name was Jingshu.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏，好學，頗有人倫鑒。

translations.literal: From childhood he was clever and keen, fond of learning, and had considerable insight into men's characters.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was clever and quick, fond of learning, and had considerable insight into men's characters.

sentences.zh: 初為本州主簿，稍遷別駕、武都郡守、鎮遠將軍、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At first he was Chief Clerk of his native province, then was gradually transferred to Administrative Aide, Prefect of Wudu Commandery, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Chief Clerk of his native province, then was gradually transferred to Administrative Aide, Prefect of Wudu Commandery, General Who Pacifies the Distance, and Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with the Golden Seal.

sentences.zh: 及周文帝為丞相，引為府屬，甚見親待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wen of Zhou was Chancellor, he brought Rang in as a staff member and treated him with great intimacy.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wen of Zhou served as Chancellor, he brought Rang in as a staff member and treated him with great intimacy.

sentences.zh: 出為衛將軍、南汾州刺史，有善政。

translations.literal: He went out as Guard General and Governor of Southern Fenzhou, with good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as Guard General and Governor of Southern Fenzhou and governed well.

sentences.zh: 尋卒官。

translations.literal: Soon he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he died in office.

sentences.zh: 贈車騎大將軍、儀同三司、涇州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Governor of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously granted General of Chariots and Cavalry, Equal Honor to the Three Ducal Ministers, and Governor of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 論曰：周惠達見禮寶夤，遂契闊於戎寇，不以夷險易志，斯固篤終之士也。

translations.literal: Commentary: Zhou Huida was received with courtesy by Baoyin and then shared hardship amid military turmoil, not changing his resolve for ease or danger—he was indeed a man who held firm to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Zhou Huida was received with courtesy by Baoyin and then shared hardship amid military turmoil, not changing his resolve whether in ease or danger—he was indeed a man who held firm to the end.

sentences.zh: 周文提劍而起，百度草創，施約法之制於競逐之辰，修太平之禮於鼎峙之日，終能斫雕為樸，變奢從儉，風化既被，而下肅上尊，疆埸屢動，而內安外附，斯蓋蘇綽之力也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Zhou raised his sword and rose; every institution was newly founded. He applied simplified-law systems in days of rivalry, cultivated rituals of great peace in days of tripartite standoff, and finally could chop carved ornament into plain wood and turn luxury toward frugality; once customs were spread, inferiors were solemn and superiors honored; though borders moved repeatedly, within was calm and without was attached—this was largely the power of Su Chuo.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Zhou raised his sword and rose; every institution was newly founded. He applied simplified-law systems in days of rivalry, cultivated rituals of great peace in days of tripartite standoff, and finally could chop carved ornament into plain wood and turn luxury toward frugality; once customs were spread, inferiors were solemn and superiors honored; though borders moved repeatedly, within was calm and without was attached—this was largely the work of Su Chuo.

sentences.zh: 邳公周道雲季，方事幽貞，隋室龍興，首應旌命。

translations.literal: Duke of Pi; the Zhou Way waned through successive reigns; just as he upheld reclusion and integrity, the Sui house rose like a dragon and he was first to answer the imperial summons.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Pi: the Zhou Way waned through successive reigns; just as he upheld reclusion and integrity, the Sui house rose like a dragon and he was first to answer the imperial summons.

sentences.zh: 綢繆任遇，窮極寵榮，久處機衡，多所損益，罄竭心力，知無不為。

translations.literal: He was bound in assignment and favor to the utmost of glory; long in the pivot of power, he made many additions and subtractions, exhausted heart and strength, and did whatever he knew to do.
translations.idiomatic: He was bound in assignment and favor to the utmost of glory; long at the pivot of power, he made many additions and subtractions, exhausted heart and strength, and did whatever he knew to do.

sentences.zh: 然志尚清儉，體非弘廣，好同惡異，有乖直道，不存易簡，未為通德。

translations.literal: Yet his aspiration favored purity and frugality while his substance was not broad and expansive; he favored agreement and hated difference, departing from the straight path; he did not uphold simplicity and ease—not comprehensive virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet his aspiration favored purity and frugality while his substance was not broad and expansive; he favored agreement and hated difference, departing from the straight path; he did not uphold simplicity and ease, and so fell short of comprehensive virtue.

sentences.zh: 曆事二帝，三十餘年，雖廢黜當時，終稱遺老。

translations.literal: He served two emperors for more than thirty years; though dismissed in his own day, in the end he was called an elder of former times.
translations.idiomatic: He served two emperors for more than thirty years; though dismissed in his own day, in the end he was still called an elder of former times.

sentences.zh: 君邪而不能正言，國亡而情均眾庶，予違汝弼，徒聞其語，疾風勁草，未見其人。

translations.literal: When the ruler was wicked he could not speak straight; when the state perished his feelings matched the common crowd; "When I err, correct me"—only his words were heard; in strong wind and stiff grass, the man himself was not seen.
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler was wicked he could not speak straight; when the state perished his sentiments matched those of the common crowd; "When I err, correct me"—only his words were heard; in strong wind and stiff grass, the man himself was not seen.

sentences.zh: 禮命闕于興王，抑亦此之由也。

translations.literal: The lack of ceremonial appointment under the founding king arose largely from this.
translations.idiomatic: The lack of ceremonial appointment under the founding king arose largely from this cause.

sentences.zh: 夔志識沈敏，方雅可稱，若天假之年，足以不虧堂構矣。

translations.literal: Kui's intent and discernment were deep and quick, his bearing and elegance worthy of praise; had Heaven granted him more years, he would have been enough not to shame the hall's frame.
translations.idiomatic: Kui's intent and discernment were deep and quick, his bearing and elegance worthy of praise; had Heaven granted him more years, he would have been enough not to shame the family estate.
